title.zh: 卷一百七十三 列傳第一百二十三: 鄭覃 陳夷行 李紳 吳汝納 李回 李珏 李固言
title.en: Volume 173 Biographies 123: Zheng Tan, Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Wu Runa, Li Hui, Li Jue, Li Guyan
title.raw: 卷一百七十三 列傳第一百二十三: 鄭覃 陳夷行 李紳 吳汝納 李回 李珏 李固言 Volume 173 Biographies 123: Zheng Tan, Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Wu Runa, Li Hui, Li Jue, Li Guyan

sentences.zh: 鄭覃，故相珣瑜之子。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan was the son of the former Chancellor Zheng Xunyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan was a son of the late Chancellor Zheng Xunyu.

sentences.zh: 以父廕補弘文校理，歷拾遺、補闕、考功員外郎、刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was appointed Collator at the Hongwen Institute, and successively served as Reminder, Supplementation Official, Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: By his father's yin privilege he entered service as collator at the Hongwen Institute, then served in turn as remonstrance reminder, supplementation official, assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel, and director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年二月，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, he was transferred to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanhe 14 he was promoted to grand censor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗用內官五人為京西北和糴使，覃上疏論罷。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong employed five inner-court eunuchs as Commissioners for Harmonious Grain Purchase in the northwest of the capital; Tan submitted a memorial arguing for their abolition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong appointed five eunuchs as commissioners for grain purchases northwest of the capital, Tan memorialized urging that the arrangement be abolished.

sentences.zh: 穆宗不恤政事，喜遊宴；

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong paid no heed to government affairs and delighted in excursions and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong neglected state affairs and delighted in pleasure outings and feasts.

sentences.zh: 即位之始，吐蕃寇邊，覃與同職崔玄亮等廷奏曰：「陛下即位已來，宴樂過多，畋遊無度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his reign, when Tibetans raided the borders, Tan together with his colleague Cui Xuanliang and others submitted a court memorial saying: "Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, feasting and music have been excessive and hunting excursions without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign, when Tibetans raided the frontier, Tan and his fellow remonstrators including Cui Xuanliang addressed the throne: "Since Your Majesty took the throne, feasting and music have been excessive, and hunting has known no bounds.

sentences.zh: 今蕃寇在境，緩急奏報，不知乘輿所在。

translations.literal: Now the barbarian raiders are at the frontier, yet for urgent and routine reports we do not know where the imperial carriage may be.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is at the border, yet for urgent and routine reports we do not know where the imperial carriage may be found.

sentences.zh: 臣等忝備諫官，不勝憂惕，伏願稍減遊縱，留心政道。

translations.literal: We, your subjects, hold the post of remonstrating officials and cannot bear our anxiety; we humbly wish that you would slightly reduce your excursions and apply your mind to the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: We who hold the post of remonstrating officials are overcome with anxiety and humbly beg that Your Majesty slightly curb these excursions and turn your attention to the business of government.

sentences.zh: 伏聞陛下晨夜昵狎倡優；

translations.literal: We have heard that Your Majesty day and night keeps intimate company with entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that day and night Your Majesty keeps close company with actors and musicians.

sentences.zh: 近習之徒，賞賜太厚。

translations.literal: Those in your immediate circle receive rewards far too lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Those in your immediate entourage receive rewards far too lavish.

sentences.zh: 凡金銀貨幣，皆出自生靈膏血，不可使無功之人，濫沾賜與。

translations.literal: All gold, silver, and currency issues from the very lifeblood of the people—it must not be that men without merit should lavishly share in gifts and grants.
translations.idiomatic: All gold, silver, and currency come from the lifeblood of the people; men without merit must not be allowed to share lavishly in gifts and grants.

sentences.zh: 縱內藏有余，亦乞用之有節，如邊上警急，即支用無闕。

translations.literal: Even if the inner treasury has surplus, we still beg that it be used with restraint, so that if the frontier should face sudden alarm, disbursements would not fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the inner treasury has surplus, we beg that it be spent with restraint, so that if the frontier faces sudden alarm, funds will not run short.

sentences.zh: 免令有司重斂百姓，實天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Spare the responsible officials from imposing heavy levies on the common people—this would truly be the good fortune of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Spare the responsible officials from imposing heavy levies on the people—this would truly be the good fortune of the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝初不悅其言，顧宰相蕭俛曰：「此輩何人？」

translations.literal: The emperor at first was displeased with their words and turned to Chancellor Xiao Mian, saying: "Who are this lot?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first took offense at their words and turned to Chancellor Xiao Mian: "Who are these people?"

sentences.zh: 俛對曰：「諫官也。」

translations.literal: Xiao replied: "They are remonstrating officials."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao replied: "They are remonstrating officials."

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解，乃曰：「朕之過失，臣下盡規，忠也。」

translations.literal: The emperor's mood eased somewhat, and he said: "When subjects fully admonish me regarding my faults, that is loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mood eased somewhat, and he said: "When my subjects fully remonstrate with me about my faults, that is loyalty."

sentences.zh: 乃謂覃曰：「閣中奏事，殊不從容。

translations.literal: He then said to Tan: "Memorials submitted through the chamber offices are quite lacking in composure.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Tan: "Memorials submitted through the chamber offices lack all composure.

sentences.zh: 今後有事面陳，朕與卿延英相見。」

translations.literal: From now on when there are matters, present them in person—I shall meet with you in the Yanying Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter when there are matters, present them in person; I shall meet with you in the Yanying Hall."

sentences.zh: 時久無閣中奏事，覃等抗論，人皆相賀。

translations.literal: At that time memorials through the chamber offices had long been absent; Tan and the others had argued forcefully, and everyone congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials through the chamber offices had long been absent; Tan and the others had spoken boldly, and everyone congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 鎮冀節度使王承宗死，其弟承元聽朝旨，移授鄭滑節度。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong, Military Governor of Zhenji, died; his younger brother Chengyuan obeyed the court's command and was transferred to serve as Military Governor of Zheng and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong, military governor of Zhenji, died; his younger brother Chengyuan obeyed the court and was transferred to the post of military governor of Zheng and Hua.

sentences.zh: 鎮之三軍留承元，以難不能赴鎮；

translations.literal: The three armies of the garrison detained Chengyuan, so that he could not go to his post because of the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies of the garrison detained Chengyuan, and he could not take up his post because of the difficulty.

sentences.zh: 承元乞重臣宣諭，乃以覃為宣諭使，起居舍人王璠副之。

translations.literal: Chengyuan requested that a senior minister be sent to proclaim the imperial will; Tan was appointed Imperial Envoy for Proclamation, with Attendant of the Gazette Wang Fan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan asked that a senior minister be sent to proclaim the imperial will; Tan was appointed imperial envoy for proclamation, with court diarist Wang Fan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮卒辭語不遜，覃至宣詔，諭以大義，軍人釋然聽命。

translations.literal: Initially the soldiers of the garrison used disrespectful language; when Tan arrived to proclaim the edict and instructed them in the greater principles, the troops calmly accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: At first the garrison soldiers spoke insolently; when Tan arrived to proclaim the edict and instructed them in the greater principles, the troops calmly accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年十一月，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Changqing, he was transferred to Supervisor of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Changqing 1 he was transferred to supervisor of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷御史中丞，十一月，權知工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and in the eleventh month was given provisional charge as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief; in the eleventh month he was given provisional charge as vice minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli, he was appointed Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoli 1 he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was reassigned as Left Regular Attendant of the Palatial Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was reassigned as left regular attendant of the palatial insignia.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he served in his existing rank as Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served in his existing rank as Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, fourth month, he was appointed vice minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 覃長於經學，稽古守正，帝尤重之。

translations.literal: Tan excelled in classical studies, investigated antiquity and held to rectitude, and the emperor especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan excelled in classical learning, investigated antiquity and held to rectitude, and the emperor especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 覃從容奏曰：「經籍訛謬，博士相沿，難為改正。

translations.literal: Tan calmly submitted: "The canonical texts contain errors that the Erudites have transmitted one after another—difficult to correct.
translations.idiomatic: Tan calmly submitted: "The canonical texts contain errors that the erudites have handed down one after another, and they are difficult to correct.

sentences.zh: 請召宿儒奧學，校定六籍；

translations.literal: Please summon venerable scholars of profound learning to collate the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that venerable scholars of profound learning be summoned to collate the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 準後漢故事，勒石於太學，永代作則，以正其闕。」

translations.literal: Following the precedent of Later Han, inscribe them on stone at the Imperial Academy to serve as a standard for all generations and rectify their lacunae."
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of Later Han, have them carved on stone at the Imperial Academy as a standard for all generations and to rectify their lacunae."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，李宗閔、牛僧孺輔政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru assisted in government.

sentences.zh: 宗閔以覃與李德裕相善，薄之。

translations.literal: Zongmin, because Tan was on good terms with Li Deyu, held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin held Tan in low esteem because Tan was on good terms with Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 時德裕自浙西入朝，復為閔、孺所排，出鎮蜀川。

translations.literal: At that time Deyu had entered court from Zhexi and was again pushed aside by Zongmin and Sengru, being sent out to govern Shuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deyu had come to court from Zhexi and was again pushed aside by Zongmin and Sengru and sent out to govern Shuchuan.

sentences.zh: 宗閔惡覃禁中言事，奏為工部尚書，罷侍講學士。

translations.literal: Zongmin disliked Tan's speaking on affairs within the Forbidden Quarter and had him appointed Minister of Public Works, removing him from his lectureship in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin disliked Tan's speaking on affairs within the inner palace and had him appointed minister of public works, removing him from his Hanlin lectureship.

sentences.zh: 文宗好經義，心頗思之。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved the meaning of the Classics and in his heart greatly missed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved the meaning of the Classics and greatly missed him.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，復召為侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year he was again summoned as Lecturer in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he was again summoned as Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 七年春，德裕作相。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Deyu became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year Deyu became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 五月，以覃為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Tan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tan was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗於延英謂宰相曰：「殷侑通經學，為人頗似鄭覃。」

translations.literal: Wenzong once said to the chancellors in the Yanying Hall: "Yin You is versed in classical learning and in character is rather like Zheng Tan."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong once said to the chancellors in the Yanying Hall: "Yin You is versed in classical learning and in character is rather like Zheng Tan."

sentences.zh: 宗閔曰：「覃、侑誠有經學，於議論不足聽覽。」

translations.literal: Zongmin said: "Tan and You truly have classical learning, but their discourse is not worth hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin said: "Tan and You truly have classical learning, but their discourse is not worth listening to."

sentences.zh: 李德裕對曰：「殷、鄭之言，他人不欲聞，唯陛下切欲聞之。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu replied: "The words of Yin and Zheng—others do not wish to hear them, yet Your Majesty earnestly wishes to hear them."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu replied: "The words of Yin and Zheng are what others do not wish to hear, yet Your Majesty earnestly wishes to hear them.

sentences.zh: 覃嘗嫉人朋黨，為宗閔所薄故也。

translations.literal: Tan had often detested factional cliques—hence Zongmin's disdain for him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had often detested factional cliques—hence Zongmin's disdain for him.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 其年，德裕罷相，宗閔復知政，與李訓、鄭註同排斥李德裕、李紳。

translations.literal: That year Deyu was dismissed as chancellor; Zongmin again took charge of government and, together with Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, jointly pushed aside Li Deyu and Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: That year Deyu was dismissed as chancellor; Zongmin again took charge of government and, together with Li Xun and Zheng Zhu, jointly pushed aside Li Deyu and Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 二人貶黜，覃亦左授秘書監。

translations.literal: When the two were demoted and banished, Tan too was demoted and appointed as Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When the two were demoted and banished, Tan too was demoted and appointed director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，楊虞卿、李宗閔得罪長流，復以覃為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Yang Yuqing and Li Zongmin were found guilty and banished to distant places; Tan was again appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year Yang Yuqing and Li Zongmin were found guilty and banished to distant places; Tan was again appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十月，遷尚書右僕射，兼判國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently given charge of the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to right vice director of the secretariat and concurrently given charge of chancellor of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 訓、註伏誅，召覃入禁中草制敕，明日以本官同平章事，封滎陽郡公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Xun and Zhu were executed, Tan was summoned into the Forbidden Quarter to draft edicts; the next day, with his existing office he was made Associate Counselor, enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun and Zhu were executed, Tan was summoned into the inner palace to draft edicts; the next day, retaining his existing office, he was made associate counselor, enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 覃雖精經義，不能為文。

translations.literal: Although Tan was expert in the meaning of the Classics, he could not compose literary prose.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tan was expert in the meaning of the Classics, he could not compose literary prose.

sentences.zh: 嫉進士浮華。

translations.literal: He detested the flamboyance of the jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He detested the flamboyance of jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 開成初，奏禮部貢院宜罷進士科。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kai Cheng he memorialized that the Ministry of Rites examination grounds should abolish the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kai Cheng he memorialized that the Ministry of Rites examination grounds should abolish the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 初，紫宸對，上語及選士，覃曰：「南北朝多用文華，所以不治。

translations.literal: Initially, during an audience in the Zichen Hall, the emperor spoke of selecting officials; Tan said: "The Northern and Southern Dynasties relied heavily on literary ornament—hence their failure to achieve good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, during an audience in the Zichen Hall, the emperor spoke of selecting officials; Tan said: "The Northern and Southern Dynasties relied heavily on literary ornament, and that is why they failed to achieve good governance.

sentences.zh: 士以才堪即用，何必文辭？」

translations.literal: Officials should be employed as soon as their talent qualifies them—why must there be literary polish?"
translations.idiomatic: Officials should be employed as soon as their talent qualifies them—why must there be literary polish?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「進士及第人已曾為州縣官者，方鎮奏署即可之，余即否。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jinshi who have passed the examination and have already served as officials in prefectures and districts—for these, when military governors recommend them for appointments, I may approve; for the rest, no."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Jinshi who have passed the examination and have already served as officials in prefectures and districts—for these, when military governors recommend them for appointments, I may approve; for the rest, no."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「此科率多輕薄，不必盡用。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "This examination track is mostly frivolous men—not all need be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "This examination track is mostly frivolous men—not all need be employed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「輕薄敦厚，色色有之，未必獨在進士。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Frivolity and solid character exist in every sort—not necessarily only among jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Frivolity and solid character exist in every sort—not necessarily only among jinshi.

sentences.zh: 此科置已二百年，亦不可遽改。」

translations.literal: This examination has been established for two hundred years—it cannot be abruptly changed."
translations.idiomatic: This examination has been established for two hundred years—it cannot be abruptly changed."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「亦不可過有崇樹。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "Nor should it be excessively honored and promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Nor should it be excessively honored and promoted."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂宰臣曰：「百司弛慢，要重條舉。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to the chancellors: "The hundred offices are lax and sluggish—we must seriously enforce regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to the chancellors: "The hundred offices are lax and sluggish—we must seriously enforce regulations."

sentences.zh: 因指香爐曰：「此爐始亦華好，用之既久，乃無光彩。

translations.literal: Indicating an incense burner, he said: "This burner was at first also splendid and fine, but after long use it has lost its luster.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to an incense burner, he said: "This burner was at first splendid and fine, but after long use it has lost its luster.

sentences.zh: 若不加飾，何由復初？」

translations.literal: If it is not refurbished, how can it return to its original state?"
translations.idiomatic: If it is not refurbished, how can it return to its original state?"

sentences.zh: 覃對曰：「丕變風俗，當考實效。

translations.literal: Tan replied: "To greatly transform customs, one should examine actual results.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied: "To greatly transform customs, one should examine actual results.

sentences.zh: 自三十年已來，多不務實，取於顏情。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years most have not pursued substance but have sought to please the eye.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years most have not pursued substance but have sought to please the eye.

sentences.zh: 如嵇、阮之流，不攝職事。」

translations.literal: Men like Ji Kang and Ruan Ji did not attend to their official duties."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ji Kang and Ruan Ji did not attend to their official duties."

sentences.zh: 李石云：「此本因治平，人人無事，安逸所致。

translations.literal: Li Shi said: "This originally arose because under a peaceful reign everyone had nothing to do—leisure and ease brought it about.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi said: "This originally arose because under a peaceful reign everyone had nothing to do—leisure and ease brought it about.

sentences.zh: 今之人俗亦慕王夷甫，恥不能及之。」

translations.literal: Today's popular customs also admire Wang Yifu and shame themselves for failing to match him."
translations.idiomatic: Today's popular customs also admire Wang Yifu and shame themselves for failing to match him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿等輔朕，在振舉法度而已。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You who assist me need only rouse and uphold the laws and standards."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You who assist me need only rouse and uphold the laws and standards."

sentences.zh: 時太學勒石經，覃奏起居郎周墀、水部員外郎崔球、監察御史張次宗、禮部員外郎溫業等，校定《九經》文字，旋令上石。

translations.literal: At that time the Imperial Academy was inscribing stone classics; Tan memorialized that Attendant Zhou Chi, Assistant Director of the Ministry of Water Cui Qiu, Investigating Censor Zhang Cizong, Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites Wen Ye, and others should collate the text of the Nine Classics and then have it carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Imperial Academy was inscribing stone classics; Tan memorialized that Attendant Zhou Chi, assistant director of the Ministry of Water Cui Qiu, investigating censor Zhang Cizong, assistant director of the Ministry of Rites Wen Ye, and others should collate the text of the Nine Classics and then have it carved on stone.

sentences.zh: 加門下侍郎、弘文館大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Vice Director in the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute, with supervision of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed vice director in the secretariat, grand academician of the Hongwen Institute, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 上嘗於延英論古今詩句工拙，覃曰：「孔子所刪，三百篇是也。

translations.literal: The emperor once in the Yanying Hall discussed the skill or clumsiness of ancient and modern poetic lines; Tan said: "What Confucius edited—the three hundred pieces—is it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once in the Yanying Hall discussed the skill or clumsiness of ancient and modern poetic lines; Tan said: "What Confucius edited—the three hundred pieces—is it.

sentences.zh: 降此五言七言，辭非雅正，不足帝王賞詠。

translations.literal: Beneath these, the five-character and seven-character forms—their wording is not elegant and correct and are not worthy of imperial appreciation and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath these, the five-character and seven-character forms—their wording is not elegant and correct and are not worthy of imperial appreciation and recitation.

sentences.zh: 夫《詩》之《雅》、《頌》，皆下刺上所為，非上化下而作。

translations.literal: As for the Ya and Song sections of the Odes—they were all made by subjects below to admonish the ruler above; they were not composed by the ruler to transform those below.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Ya and Song sections of the Odes—they were all made by subjects below to admonish the ruler above; they were not composed by the ruler to transform those below.

sentences.zh: 王者采詩，以考風俗得失。

translations.literal: The king collected songs to examine whether customs were flourishing or failing.
translations.idiomatic: The king collected songs to examine whether customs were flourishing or failing.

sentences.zh: 仲尼刪定，以為世規。

translations.literal: Confucius edited and fixed them to serve as a standard for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius edited and fixed them to serve as a standard for the age.

sentences.zh: 近代陳後主、隋煬帝皆能章句，不知王者大端，終有季年之失。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Houzhu of Chen and Emperor Yang of Sui could both parse verses line by line, yet did not understand the great essentials of kingship, and in the end met the failures of their declining years.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Houzhu of Chen and Emperor Yang of Sui could both parse verses line by line, yet did not understand the great essentials of kingship, and in the end met the failures of their declining years.

sentences.zh: 章句小道，願陛下不取也。」

translations.literal: Parsing verses is a petty path—I beg Your Majesty not to pursue it."
translations.idiomatic: Parsing verses is a petty path—I beg Your Majesty not to pursue it.

sentences.zh: 覃以宰相兼判國子祭酒，奏太學置五經博士各一人，緣無職田，請依王府官例，賜祿粟。

translations.literal: As chancellor Tan also concurrently supervised the Directorate of Education; he memorialized that the Imperial Academy should establish one Erudite for each of the Five Classics, and because they had no official field allotments, requested that grain and salary be granted following the precedent for officials of the princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Tan also concurrently supervised the directorate of education; he memorialized that the Imperial Academy should establish one erudite for each of the Five Classics, and because they had no official field allotments, requested that grain and salary be granted following the precedent for officials of the princely establishments.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又進《石壁九經》一百六十卷。

translations.literal: He also presented the Stone Wall Nine Classics in one hundred sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented the Stone Wall Nine Classics in one hundred sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 其年，李固言復為宰相。

translations.literal: That year Li Guyan again became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Guyan again became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 固言與李宗閔、楊嗣復善，覃憎之。

translations.literal: Guyan was on good terms with Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu, and Tan detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan was on good terms with Li Zongmin and Yang Sifu, and Tan detested him.

sentences.zh: 因起居郎闕，固言奏曰：「周敬復、崔球、張次宗等三人，皆堪此任。」

translations.literal: When the post of Attendant of the Gazette fell vacant, Guyan memorialized: "Zhou Jingfu, Cui Qiu, and Zhang Cizong—all three are fit for this office."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of attendant of the gazette fell vacant, Guyan memorialized: "Zhou Jingfu, Cui Qiu, and Zhang Cizong—all three are fit for this office."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「崔球遊宗閔之門，且赤墀下秉筆，為千古法，不可朋黨。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Cui Qiu frequents Zongmin's circle, and moreover beneath the Red Terrace he holds the brush—this sets the standard for a thousand generations; factional ties cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Cui Qiu frequents Zongmin's circle, and moreover beneath the Red Terrace he holds the brush—this sets the standard for a thousand generations; factional ties cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 如裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有纖芥異論。」

translations.literal: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, your subject would not venture the slightest dissent."
translations.idiomatic: As for Pei Zhongru and Li Rangyi, your subject would not venture the slightest dissent.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 三年，楊嗣復自西川入拜平章事，與覃尤相矛盾；

translations.literal: In the third year Yang Sifu entered court from Xichuan and was appointed Associate Counselor; he was especially at odds with Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yang Sifu entered court from Xichuan and was appointed associate counselor; he was especially at odds with Tan.

sentences.zh: 加之以固言、李玨，入對之際，是非蜂起。

translations.literal: With Guyan and Li Jue added in, whenever they entered to respond to the throne, disputes swarmed like hornets.
translations.idiomatic: With Guyan and Li Jue added in, whenever they entered to respond to the throne, disputes swarmed like hornets.

sentences.zh: 二月，覃進位太子太師。

translations.literal: In the second month Tan was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Tan was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文宗以旱放系囚，出宮人劉好奴等五百余人，送兩街寺觀，任歸親戚。

translations.literal: Because of drought Wenzong released prisoners in custody and released more than five hundred palace women including Liu Haonu, sending them to Buddhist and Daoist temples on the two avenues to return to their kin as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Because of drought Wenzong released prisoners in custody and released more than five hundred palace women including Liu Haonu, sending them to Buddhist and Daoist temples on the two avenues to return to their kin as they wished.

sentences.zh: 紫宸對，李玨曰：「陛下放宮女數多，德邁千古。

translations.literal: At an audience in the Zichen Hall, Li Jue said: "Your Majesty has released a great many palace women—your virtue surpasses a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience in the Zichen Hall, Li Jue said: "Your Majesty has released a great many palace women—your virtue surpasses a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 漢制，八月選人，晉武平吳，亦多采擇。

translations.literal: Under Han institutions, in the eighth month women were selected; when Jin Wu pacified Wu, he also took many in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han institutions, in the eighth month women were selected; when Jin Wu pacified Wu, he also took many in selection.

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂『未見好德如好色』。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'I have not seen one who loved virtue as he loved beauty.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'I have not seen one who loved virtue as he loved beauty.'

sentences.zh: 今陛下以為無益放之，微臣敢賀。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty holds them of no benefit and releases them—this humble subject dares to offer congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty holds them of no benefit and releases them—this humble subject dares to offer congratulations."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「晉武帝以采擇之失，中原化為左衽；

translations.literal: Tan said: "Jin Wudi because of the fault of excessive selection—the Central Plains were transformed to wearing garments buttoned on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Jin Wudi because of the fault of excessive selection—the Central Plains were transformed to wearing garments buttoned on the left.

sentences.zh: 陛下以為殷鑒，放去攸宜。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes this as a mirror of warning—how fitting to release them."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes this as a mirror of warning—how fitting to release them.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，三上章求罷，詔落太子太師，余如故。

translations.literal: That year, in the twelfth month, he thrice submitted memorials requesting to resign; an edict removed him from Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent while the rest of his offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the twelfth month, he thrice submitted memorials requesting to resign; an edict removed him from grand tutor of the heir apparent while the rest of his offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 仍三五日一入中書，商量政事。

translations.literal: He still entered the Secretariat once every three or five days to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He still came to the Secretariat every few days to discuss government business.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，罷相，守左僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was dismissed as chancellor and retained as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he left the chancellorship and remained as left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，李德裕用事，欲援為宰相。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Li Deyu held power and wished to support him as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Li Deyu was in charge and wanted to bring him back as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 固以足疾不任朝謁。

translations.literal: He firmly pleaded foot ailment and inability to attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly pleaded a foot ailment that left him unable to attend court audiences.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，守司徒致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he retired as Minister of Works and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 2 he retired as minister of works and died.

sentences.zh: 子裔綽，以廕授渭南尉，直弘文館。

translations.literal: His son Yichuo was appointed Wei of Weinan by yin privilege and served at the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yichuo entered service by yin privilege as wei of Weinan and served on duty at the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 覃少清苦貞退，不造次與人款狎。

translations.literal: From youth Tan endured poverty, hardship, integrity, and retirement; he did not casually become intimate with others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tan lived in plain poverty and upright seclusion and did not casually become familiar with others.

sentences.zh: 位至相國，所居未嘗增飾，才庇風雨。

translations.literal: Even after reaching the rank of chancellor, his residence was never embellished—barely enough to shelter from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose to chancellor, his home was never improved beyond what barely kept out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 家無媵妾，人皆仰其素風。

translations.literal: His household had no concubines, and all admired his plain character.
translations.idiomatic: His household kept no concubines, and everyone admired his unadorned way of life.

sentences.zh: 然嫉惡太過，多所不容，眾憚而惡之。

translations.literal: Yet his hatred of evil was excessive and many could not be tolerated; the multitude feared and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he hated evil to excess and would tolerate little; many feared and resented him.

sentences.zh: 覃弟朗、潛。

translations.literal: Tan had younger brothers Lang and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brothers were Lang and Qian.

sentences.zh: 朗，字有融。

translations.literal: Lang, styled Yourong.
translations.idiomatic: Lang, whose style was Yourong.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，登進士甲科，再遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he passed the jinshi examination in the top tier and was twice promoted to Right Remonstrance Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 1 he passed the jinshi examination in the top tier and was promoted twice to right remonstrance reminder.

sentences.zh: 開成中，為起居郎。

translations.literal: During Kai Cheng he served as Attendant of the Gazette.
translations.idiomatic: During Kai Cheng he served as attendant of the gazette.

sentences.zh: 初，太和末風俗稍奢，文宗恭勤節儉，冀革其風。

translations.literal: Initially, at the end of Taihe, customs had become somewhat lavish; Wenzong was respectfully diligent and frugal, hoping to reform this trend.
translations.idiomatic: At first, toward the end of Taihe, customs had grown somewhat extravagant; Wenzong was respectful, diligent, and frugal, hoping to change the trend.

sentences.zh: 宰臣等言曰：「陛下節儉省用，風俗已移，長裾大袂，漸以減損。

translations.literal: The chancellors and others said: "Your Majesty's frugality and economy have already shifted customs; long skirts and wide sleeves are gradually being reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors said: "Your Majesty's thrift and restraint have already begun to shift customs; long skirts and wide sleeves are gradually disappearing.

sentences.zh: 若更令戚屬絕其侈靡，不慮下不從教。」

translations.literal: If you further require your kin to end their extravagance, there is no worry that those below will not follow instruction."
translations.idiomatic: If you further require your kin to abandon extravagance, there is no reason to fear that those below will not follow your teaching."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此事亦難戶曉，但去其泰甚，自以儉德化之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This matter is also hard to make clear to every household; one need only remove what is excessive and transform people through the virtue of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is also hard to explain to every household; one need only remove what is excessive and transform people through the virtue of frugality.

sentences.zh: 朕聞前時內庫唯二錦袍，飾以金鳥，一袍玄宗幸溫湯禦之，一即與貴妃。

translations.literal: I have heard that in former times the inner treasury had only two brocade robes adorned with golden birds—one robe Emperor Xuanzong wore when he visited the hot springs, and one he gave to the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in former times the inner treasury held only two brocade robes adorned with golden birds—one that Emperor Xuanzong wore when he visited the hot springs, and one that he gave to the Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 當時貴重如此，如今奢靡，豈復貴之？

translations.literal: At that time they were valued so highly—now with such extravagance, how could they still be prized?
translations.idiomatic: At that time they were prized so highly—now, with such extravagance everywhere, how could they still be prized?

sentences.zh: 料今富家往往皆有。

translations.literal: I expect that wealthy families today often all have them.
translations.idiomatic: I expect that wealthy families today often have them as well.

sentences.zh: 左衛副使張元昌便用金唾壺，昨因李訓，已誅之矣。」

translations.literal: Deputy Commander of the Left Guard Zhang Yuanchang casually used a golden spittoon; yesterday because of Li Xun he has already been executed."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander of the Left Guard Zhang Yuanchang casually used a golden spittoon; yesterday, because of Li Xun, he was already executed.

sentences.zh: 時朗執筆螭頭下，宰臣退，上謂朗曰：「適所議論，卿記錄未？

translations.literal: At that time Lang held the brush beneath the imperial seat; after the chancellors withdrew, the emperor said to Lang: "The discussion just now—have you recorded it?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lang held the brush beneath the imperial seat; after the chancellors withdrew, the emperor said to Lang: "The discussion just now—have you recorded it?

sentences.zh: 吾試觀之。」

translations.literal: I wish to look at it."
translations.idiomatic: Let me see it."

sentences.zh: 朗對曰：「臣執筆所記，便名為史。

translations.literal: Lang replied: "What your subject records with the brush is called history.
translations.idiomatic: Lang replied: "What I record with the brush is called history.

sentences.zh: 伏準故事，帝王不可取觀。

translations.literal: According to precedent, an emperor may not take and view it.
translations.idiomatic: According to precedent, an emperor may not take and view it.

sentences.zh: 昔太宗欲覽國史，諫議大夫硃子奢云：『史官所述，不隱善惡。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Taizong wished to read the national history, Remonstrance Grand Censor Zhu Zixia said: 'What the historiographers record does not conceal good or evil.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Emperor Taizong wished to read the national history, remonstrance grand censor Zhu Zixia said: 'What the historiographers record does not conceal good or evil.

sentences.zh: 或主非上智，飾非護失，見之則致怨，所以義不可觀。』

translations.literal: If a ruler is not of the highest wisdom, he may gloss over faults and shield errors; seeing the record would provoke resentment—therefore by principle it may not be viewed.'
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler is not of the highest wisdom, he may gloss over faults and shield errors; seeing the record would provoke resentment—therefore by principle it may not be viewed.'

sentences.zh: 又褚遂良曰：『今之起居郎，古之左右史也；

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang also said: 'Today's Attendant of the Gazette is the ancient Left and Right Historiographer;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang also said: 'Today's attendant of the gazette is the ancient left and right historiographer;

sentences.zh: 記人君言行，善惡必書，庶幾不為非法，不聞帝王躬自觀史。』」

translations.literal: he records the ruler's words and deeds, and good and evil must be written, so that he may not act unlawfully—I have never heard of an emperor personally viewing the history.
translations.idiomatic: he records the ruler's words and deeds, and good and evil must be written, so that the ruler may not act unlawfully—I have never heard of an emperor personally viewing the history.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「適來所記，無可否臧，見亦何爽？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What was just recorded has no approval or blame—what harm in seeing it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What was just recorded has no approval or blame—what harm would there be in seeing it?"

sentences.zh: 乃宣謂宰臣曰：「鄭朗引故事，不欲脫見起居註。

translations.literal: He then announced to the chancellors: "Zheng Lang cited precedent and did not wish to let me see the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He then announced to the chancellors: "Zheng Lang cited precedent and did not wish to let me see the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 夫人君之言，善惡必書。

translations.literal: A ruler's words—good and evil must be written.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's words—good and evil must be written down.

sentences.zh: 朕恐平常閑話，不關理體，垂諸將來，竊以為恥。

translations.literal: I fear that ordinary idle talk, unrelated to principle, if handed down to future generations, would privately be a shame.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that ordinary idle talk, unrelated to principle, if handed down to future generations, would be a private shame.

sentences.zh: 異日臨朝，庶幾稍改，何妨一見，以誡醜言。」

translations.literal: On another day when I hold court I may slightly reform myself—what harm in one viewing, to warn against ugly speech?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day when I hold court I may reform myself slightly—what harm in one viewing, to warn against ugly speech?

sentences.zh: 朗遂進之。

translations.literal: Lang then presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lang then presented it.

sentences.zh: 朗轉考功郎中。

translations.literal: Lang was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to grand censor.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，為給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he served as Supervisor of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huichang he served as supervisor of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史，入為御史中丞、戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Hua Province, entered court as Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue, and adjudicated affairs of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as prefect of Hua Province, then entered court as vice censor-in-chief and vice minister of revenue, with charge of that ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，出為定州刺史、義武軍節度、易定觀察、北平軍等使。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong reign he went out as Prefect of Ding Prefecture, Military Governor of Yiwu Army, Observation Commissioner of Yi and Ding, Commissioner of the Beiping Army, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong reign he went out as prefect of Ding, military governor of the Yiwu Army, observation commissioner of Yi and Ding, commissioner of the Beiping Army, and related posts.

sentences.zh: 尋遷檢校戶部尚書、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度、宋亳汴潁觀察等使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred as Acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Bian Prefecture, Military Governor of Xuanwu Army, and Observation Commissioner of Song, Bo, Bian, and Ying, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred as acting minister of revenue, prefect of Bian, military governor of the Xuanwu Army, and observation commissioner of Song, Bo, Bian, and Ying, and related posts.

sentences.zh: 入為工部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Public Works and adjudicated the Directorate of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as minister of public works with charge of the directorate of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫，改禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and changed to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and then changed to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 以本官同平章事，加中書侍郎、集賢殿大學士，修國史。

translations.literal: With his existing office he became Associate Counselor, was further appointed Vice Director in the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his existing office he became associate counselor, was further appointed vice director in the secretariat and grand academician of the Jixian Hall, and compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 大中十年，以疾辭位。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dazhong he resigned his office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 10 he resigned his office because of illness.

sentences.zh: 進加檢校右僕射、守太子少師。

translations.literal: He was further promoted as Acting Right Vice Director and Retained Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted as acting right vice director and retained junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict said:

sentences.zh: 故通議大夫、檢校尚書右僕射、兼太子少師、上柱國、賜紫金魚袋鄭朗，植操端方，稟氣莊重；

translations.literal: The late Grand Master for Discussion, Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Pillar of State of the Upper Rank, granted the purple-gold fish tally—Zheng Lang—upheld upright conduct and was endowed with a solemn bearing;
translations.idiomatic: The late grand master for discussion, acting right vice director of the secretariat, concurrent junior tutor of the heir apparent, pillar of state of the upper rank, granted the purple-gold fish tally—Zheng Lang—upheld upright conduct and was endowed with a solemn bearing;

sentences.zh: 藹若瑞玉，淡如澄川。

translations.literal: gentle as auspicious jade, calm as a clear stream.
translations.idiomatic: gentle as auspicious jade, calm as a clear stream.

sentences.zh: 智略合乎蓍龜，誠信服於僚友。

translations.literal: His wisdom and strategy accorded with divination by yarrow and tortoise; his sincerity and trust won over colleagues and friends.
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom and strategy accorded with divination by yarrow and tortoise; his sincerity and trust won over colleagues and friends.

sentences.zh: 自膺寵寄，頗負全才，竭匪躬於諫垣，彰盡瘁於瑣闥。

translations.literal: From the time he received imperial favor he bore full talent, exhausted himself in the remonstrance offices, and showed complete devotion in the inner gates.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he received imperial favor he bore full talent, exhausted himself in the remonstrance offices, and showed complete devotion in the inner gates.

sentences.zh: 載踐方嶽，亟登師壇。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served in regional command and quickly rose to military authority.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served in regional command and quickly rose to military authority.

sentences.zh: 觀風推惠愛之心，訓士得撫循之術。

translations.literal: In inspecting local customs he promoted a heart of kindness and love; in training soldiers he mastered the art of soothing and guiding.
translations.idiomatic: In inspecting local customs he promoted kindness and love; in training soldiers he mastered the art of soothing and guiding.

sentences.zh: 政溢聞聽，念茲征還，位冠冬卿，職重邦計。

translations.literal: His governance overflowed into public report; mindful of this he was recalled, crowned the chief of the winter ministry, and charged with the weight of the state's accounts.
translations.idiomatic: His governance overflowed into public report; mindful of this he was recalled, placed at the head of the winter ministry, and charged with the weight of the state's accounts.

sentences.zh: 經費有節，財用不虧。

translations.literal: Expenditures were kept within bounds and finances did not suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditures were kept within bounds and finances did not suffer loss.

sentences.zh: 繄彼休功，明我推擇。

translations.literal: Because of those fine achievements, I clearly chose him for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Because of those fine achievements, I clearly chose him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 爰嘉峭峻，俾總紀綱。

translations.literal: I then praised his stern uprightness and had him oversee the laws and standards.
translations.idiomatic: I then praised his stern uprightness and had him oversee the laws and standards.

sentences.zh: 公望益隆，典彜具舉；

translations.literal: His public reputation grew ever higher and canonical rites were fully upheld;
translations.idiomatic: His public reputation grew ever higher and canonical rites were fully upheld;

sentences.zh: 式諧註意，且沃深衷。

translations.literal: he harmonized with my intent and nourished my inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: he harmonized with my intent and nourished my inmost heart.

sentences.zh: 俄參化源，以提政柄。

translations.literal: Soon he joined the source of transformation and took up the handle of government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined the source of transformation and took up the handle of government.

sentences.zh: 三事仰清廉之節，百度見損益之能。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies looked up to his integrity; the hundred offices saw his capacity for improvement and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies looked up to his integrity; the hundred offices saw his capacity for improvement and reduction.

sentences.zh: 近煦和風，遠浹膏雨。

translations.literal: Near at hand he warmed like a gentle breeze; far away he moistened like nourishing rain.
translations.idiomatic: Near at hand he warmed like a gentle breeze; far away he moistened like nourishing rain.

sentences.zh: 方俟坐鎮雅俗，表率庶官，頤養或乖，腠理生疾，屢陳章疏，乞遂退閑。

translations.literal: Just as he was awaited to settle customs and serve as a model for all officials, his nourishment went awry and illness arose in his flesh; he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was awaited to settle customs and serve as a model for all officials, his nourishment went awry and illness arose; he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire in leisure.

sentences.zh: 既堅乃誠，式允其請。

translations.literal: Since his sincerity was firm, I granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Since his sincerity was firm, I granted his request.

sentences.zh: 每圖懿績，唯冀有瘳。

translations.literal: Each time I recalled his fine achievements, I only hoped for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I recalled his fine achievements, I only hoped for recovery.

sentences.zh: 何竟至於彌留，而遽聞於捐代。

translations.literal: How did it come to lingering illness, and then so suddenly to news of his death?
translations.idiomatic: How did it come to lingering illness, and then so suddenly to news of his death?

sentences.zh: 閱奏興悼，臨軒載懷。

translations.literal: Reading the memorial I was moved to mourning; facing the hall I was filled with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial I was moved to mourning; facing the hall I was filled with grief.

sentences.zh: 將輟視朝之儀，兼列上公之秩。

translations.literal: I shall suspend the ceremony of holding court and also confer the rank of upper duke.
translations.idiomatic: I shall suspend the ceremony of holding court and also confer the rank of upper duke.

sentences.zh: 慰茲幽壞，期爾有知，可贈司空。

translations.literal: To comfort him in the dark realm, expecting that he has awareness, he may be posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: To comfort him in the dark realm, expecting that he has awareness, he may be posthumously granted minister of works.

sentences.zh: 潛，字無悶，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: Qian, styled Wumen, also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, whose style was Wumen, also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 陳夷行，字周道，潁川人。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing, styled Zhou Dao, was a man of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing, whose style was Zhou Dao, was a native of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖忠，父邑。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Zhong; his father was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Zhong and his father was Yi.

sentences.zh: 夷行，元和七年登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Yixing passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Yuanhe and was repeatedly summoned to commissioner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing passed the jinshi examination in Yuanhe 7 and was repeatedly summoned to commissioner offices.

sentences.zh: 寶歷末，由侍御史改虞部員外郎，皆分務東都。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoli he was changed from Attending Censor to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Parks and all served in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Baoli he was changed from attending censor to assistant director of the Ministry of Parks, and all served in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，入為起居郎、史館修撰，預修《憲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he entered court as Attendant of the Gazette and Compiler in the History Institute, participating in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 he entered court as attendant of the gazette and compiler in the History Institute, participating in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 四年獻上，轉司封員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was submitted; he was transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was submitted; he was transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Honors.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四月，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼充皇太子侍讀，詔五日一度入長生院侍太子講經。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally appointed Lecturer to the Heir Apparent; an edict ordered him once every five days to enter the Changsheng Courtyard to lecture the heir on the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was additionally appointed lecturer to the heir apparent; an edict ordered him once every five days to enter the Changsheng Courtyard to lecture the heir on the Classics.

sentences.zh: 上召對，面賜緋衣牙笏，遷諫議大夫、知制誥，余職如故。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience and personally granted him scarlet robes and an ivory tablet; he was promoted to Grand Censor and given charge of drafting edicts, with his other offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for audience and personally granted him scarlet robes and an ivory tablet; he was promoted to grand censor and given charge of drafting edicts, with his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，改太常少卿，知制誥、學士侍講如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his charge of drafting edicts and his lectureship in the academy remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his charge of drafting edicts and his lectureship in the academy remained as before.

sentences.zh: 開成二年四月，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kai Cheng, fourth month, with his existing office he became Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kai Cheng 2, fourth month, retaining his existing office he became associate counselor.

sentences.zh: 三年，楊嗣復、李玨繼入輔政。

translations.literal: In the third year Yang Sifu and Li Jue successively entered to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yang Sifu and Li Jue successively entered to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 夷行介特，素惡其所為，每上前議政，語侵嗣復，遂至往復。

translations.literal: Yixing was upright and exceptional and had always detested their conduct; whenever he discussed government before the emperor his words encroached on Sifu, and disputes went back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing was upright and exceptional and had always detested their conduct; whenever he discussed government before the emperor his words encroached on Sifu, and disputes went back and forth.

sentences.zh: 性不能堪，上表稱足疾辭位；

translations.literal: Unable to endure it in temperament, he submitted a memorial claiming foot ailment and requesting to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure it, he submitted a memorial claiming foot ailment and requesting to resign his office.

sentences.zh: 不許，詔中使就第宣勞。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; an edict sent a palace envoy to his residence to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: This was not permitted; an edict sent a palace envoy to his residence to proclaim consolation.

sentences.zh: 七月，以王彥威為忠武節度使，史孝章為邠寧節度使，皆嗣復擬議。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wang Yanwei was appointed Military Governor of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang was appointed Military Governor of Binning—both were proposals of Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Yanwei was appointed military governor of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang was appointed military governor of Binning—both were proposals of Sifu.

sentences.zh: 因延英對，上問夷行曰：「昨除二鎮，當否？」

translations.literal: During an audience in the Yanying Hall the emperor asked Yixing: "Yesterday's appointments to the two garrisons—were they appropriate?"
translations.idiomatic: During an audience in the Yanying Hall the emperor asked Yixing: "Yesterday's appointments to the two garrisons—were they appropriate?"

sentences.zh: 夷行對曰：「但出自聖心即當。」

translations.literal: Yixing replied: "So long as they issued from the sacred heart, they are appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing replied: "So long as they issued from Your Majesty's own decision, they are appropriate."

sentences.zh: 楊嗣復曰：「若出自聖心當，即人情皆愜。

translations.literal: Yang Sifu said: "If they are appropriate because they issued from the sacred heart, then popular sentiment is all satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu said: "If they are appropriate because they issued from Your Majesty's own decision, then popular sentiment is all satisfied.

sentences.zh: 如事或過當，臣下安得無言？」

translations.literal: If the matter is perhaps excessive, how could subjects below not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: If the matter is perhaps excessive, how could subjects below not speak?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠如此，朕固無私也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If it is truly so, I am indeed without private motive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If it is truly so, I am indeed without private motive."

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「自三數年來，奸臣竊權，陛下不可倒持太阿，授人钅尊柄。」

translations.literal: Yixing said: "For the past several years treacherous ministers have stolen power; Your Majesty must not hold the sword Tai'e reversed and hand the handle to others."
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said: "For the past several years treacherous ministers have stolen power; Your Majesty must not hold the sword Tai'e reversed and hand the handle to others."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「齊桓用管仲於讎虜，豈有太阿之慮乎？」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Duke Huan of Qi employed Guan Zhong from among his enemies—was there any worry about the sword Tai'e?"
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "Duke Huan of Qi employed Guan Zhong from among his enemies—was there any worry about the sword Tai'e?

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 仙韶院樂官尉遲璋授王府率，右拾遺竇洵直當衙論曰：「伶人自有本色官，不合授之清秩。」

translations.literal: Yuchi Zhang, a musician of the Xian Shao Court, was granted Captain of the Princely Establishment; Right Remonstrance Reminder Dou Xunzhi argued at court saying: "Entertainers have their own proper offices—it is not fitting to grant them pure ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Zhang, a musician of the Xian Shao Court, was granted captain of the princely establishment; right remonstrance reminder Dou Xunzhi argued at court saying: "Entertainers have their own proper offices—it is not fitting to grant them pure ranks."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「此小事，何足當衙論列！

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "This is a small matter—what need to argue it at court!
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said: "This is a small matter—what need to argue it at court!

sentences.zh: 王府率是六品雜官，謂之清秩，與洵直得否？

translations.literal: Captain of the Princely Establishment is a sixth-rank miscellaneous office—calling it a pure rank—is Xunzhi correct?
translations.idiomatic: Captain of the princely establishment is a sixth-rank miscellaneous office—calling it a pure rank—is Xunzhi correct?

sentences.zh: 此近名也。」

translations.literal: This comes close to seeking fame."
translations.idiomatic: This borders on seeking fame."

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「嘗聞洵直幽，今當衙論一樂官，幽則有之，亦不足怪。」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "I have heard that Xunzhi is reclusive; now he argues at court over one musician—reclusiveness he has, and that is not surprising."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "I have heard that Xunzhi is reclusive; now he argues at court over one musician—reclusiveness he certainly has, and that is hardly surprising."

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「諫官當衙，只合論宰相得失，不合論樂官。

translations.literal: Yixing said: "When remonstrating officials speak at court, they should only discuss the chancellor's merits and faults—not entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said: "When remonstrating officials speak at court, they should discuss the chancellor's merits and faults, not entertainers.

sentences.zh: 然業已陳論，須與處置。

translations.literal: Yet since the matter has already been raised, it must be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the matter has already been raised, it must be dealt with.

sentences.zh: 今後樂人每七八年與轉一官，不然，則加手力課三數人。」

translations.literal: Henceforth musicians should be transferred one rank every seven or eight years; otherwise, add three or four personal attendants."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth musicians should be promoted one rank every seven or eight years; otherwise, add three or four personal attendants to their staff."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「別與一官。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Grant a different office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Give him a different office instead.

sentences.zh: 乃授光州長史，賜洵直絹百疋。

translations.literal: Zhang was then appointed Chief Administrator of Guang Prefecture, and Xunzhi was granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was then appointed chief administrator of Guang Prefecture, and Xunzhi was granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 夷行尋轉門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Yixing was soon transferred to Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing was soon transferred to vice director in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宗用郭薳為坊州刺史，右拾遺，宋邧論列，以為不可。

translations.literal: Wenzong appointed Guo Fan as Prefect of Fang Prefecture; Right Remonstrance Reminder Song Kua argued against it, deeming it inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong appointed Guo Fan as prefect of Fang Prefecture; right remonstrance reminder Song Kua argued against it, deeming it inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 既而薳坐贓。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fan was found guilty of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fan was found guilty of corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相曰：「宋邧論事可嘉，邧授官來幾時？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chancellors: "Song Kua's remonstrance was commendable—how long has Kua held his office?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the chancellors: "Song Kua's remonstrance was commendable—how long has Kua held his office?"

sentences.zh: 嗣復曰：「去年。」

translations.literal: Sifu said: "Last year."
translations.idiomatic: Sifu said: "Last year."

sentences.zh: 因曰：「諫官論事，陛下但記其姓名，稍加優獎。

translations.literal: He then said: "When remonstrating officials speak on affairs, Your Majesty need only note their names and grant slight rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He then said: "When remonstrating officials speak on affairs, Your Majesty need only note their names and grant slight rewards.

sentences.zh: 如不當，亦須令知。」

translations.literal: If they are wrong, they must also be told so."
translations.idiomatic: If they are wrong, they must also be told so."

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「諫官論事，是其本職。

translations.literal: Yixing said: "For remonstrating officials to speak on affairs is their proper duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said: "For remonstrating officials to speak on affairs is their proper duty.

sentences.zh: 若論一事即加一官，則官何由得，不免有情。」

translations.literal: If one office is granted for each matter raised, how would offices be obtained—it cannot avoid partiality."
translations.idiomatic: If one office is granted for each matter raised, how would offices be obtained? Partiality cannot be avoided."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「情固不免，理平之時，亦不可免。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Partiality indeed cannot be avoided—even in times of good order it cannot be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Partiality indeed cannot be avoided—even in times of good order it cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 上竟以夷行議論太過，恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately considered Yixing's discourse excessive, and imperial favor gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately considered Yixing's discourse excessive, and imperial favor gradually grew thin.

sentences.zh: 尋罷知政事，守吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed from charge of government affairs and retained as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dismissed from charge of government affairs and retained as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，檢校禮部尚書，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year he was appointed Acting Minister of Rites and went out as Prefect of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he was appointed acting minister of rites and went out as prefect of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 五年，武宗即位，李德裕秉政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Wuzong took the throne and Li Deyu held government.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Emperor Wuzong took the throne and Li Deyu held the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 七月自華召入，復為中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was summoned from Hua and again became Vice Director in the Secretariat and Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was summoned from Hua and again became vice director in the secretariat and associate counselor.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年十一月，檢校司空、平章事、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Huichang 3 he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, Associate Counselor, Prefect of Hezhong, and Military Governor of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Huichang 3 he was appointed acting minister of works, associate counselor, prefect of Hezhong, and military governor of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 弟玄錫、夷實，皆進士擢第。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Xuanxi and Yishi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Xuanxi and Yishi both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 玄賜又制策登科。

translations.literal: Xuanci also passed the decree examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanci also passed the decree examination.

sentences.zh: 李紳，字公垂，潤州無錫人。

translations.literal: Li Shen, styled Gongchui, was a man of Wuxi in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, whose style was Gongchui, was a native of Wuxi in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本山東著姓。

translations.literal: His clan was originally a prominent surname of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was originally a prominent surname of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 高祖敬玄，則天朝中書令，封趙國文憲公，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jingxuan served as Director in the Secretariat under Empress Wu and was enfeoffed as Duke Wenxian of Zhao; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jingxuan served as director in the secretariat under Empress Wu and was enfeoffed as Duke Wenxian of Zhao; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 祖守一，成都郫縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouyi was Magistrate of Pi County in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouyi was magistrate of Pi County in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父晤，歷金壇、烏程、晉陵三縣令，因家無錫。

translations.literal: His father Wu successively served as magistrate of Jintan, Wucheng, and Jinling, and the family settled in Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu successively served as magistrate of Jintan, Wucheng, and Jinling, and the family settled in Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 紳六歲而孤，母盧氏教以經義。

translations.literal: Shen was orphaned at six; his mother, Lady Lu, taught him the meaning of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was orphaned at six; his mother, Lady Lu, taught him the meaning of the Classics.

sentences.zh: 紳形狀眇小而精悍，能為歌詩。

translations.literal: Shen was small in stature yet keen and vigorous, and could compose songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was small in stature yet keen and vigorous, and could compose songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 鄉賦之年，諷誦多在人口。

translations.literal: In the year of the local examination, his recited compositions were on many people's lips.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the local examination, his recited compositions were on many people's lips.

sentences.zh: 元和初，登進士第，釋褐國子助教，非其好也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and upon first appointment became Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education—not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and upon first appointment became assistant instructor at the directorate of education—not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 東歸金陵，觀察使李锜愛其才，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Returning east to Jinling, Observation Commissioner Li Qi admired his talent and summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Returning east to Jinling, observation commissioner Li Qi admired his talent and summoned him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 紳以锜所為專恣，不受其書幣；

translations.literal: Shen, because Qi's conduct was arbitrary and willful, would not accept his letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, because Qi's conduct was arbitrary and willful, would not accept his letters and gifts.

sentences.zh: 锜怒，將殺紳，遁而獲免。

translations.literal: Qi grew angry and was about to kill Shen; Shen fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qi grew angry and was about to kill Shen; Shen fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 锜誅，朝廷嘉之，召拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Qi was executed, the court praised him and summoned him as Right Remonstrance Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was executed, the court praised him and summoned him as right remonstrance reminder.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，穆宗召為翰林學士，與李德裕、元稹同在禁署，時稱「三俊」，情意相善。

translations.literal: After more than a year Muzong summoned him as Hanlin Academician; together with Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen he served in the Forbidden Offices, and at the time they were called the 'Three Outstanding Men,' on friendly terms.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Muzong summoned him as Hanlin academician; together with Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen he served in the inner offices, and at the time they were called the 'Three Outstanding Men,' on friendly terms.

sentences.zh: 尋轉右補闕。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Right Supplementation Official.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to right supplementation official.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年三月，改司勛員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the third month of Changqing 1 he was changed to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Honors and given charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Changqing 1 he was changed to assistant director in the Ministry of Honors and given charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，超拜中書舍人，內職如故。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year he was exceptionally promoted to Secretariat Drafter, with his inner-court duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year he was exceptionally promoted to secretariat drafter, with his inner-court duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 俄而稹作相，尋為李逢吉教人告稹陰事；

translations.literal: Soon Zhen became chancellor, and then Li Fengji had men report Zhen's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhen became chancellor, and then Li Fengji had men report Zhen's secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 稹罷相，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen was dismissed as chancellor and sent out as Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was dismissed as chancellor and sent out as prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時德裕與牛僧孺俱有相望，德裕恩顧稍深。

translations.literal: At that time both Deyu and Niu Sengru enjoyed high repute, but Deyu's imperial favor was somewhat deeper.
translations.idiomatic: At that time both Deyu and Niu Sengru enjoyed high repute, but Deyu's imperial favor was somewhat deeper.

sentences.zh: 逢吉欲用僧孺，懼紳與德裕沮於禁中。

translations.literal: Fengji wished to employ Sengru but feared that Shen and Deyu would obstruct this within the Forbidden Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji wished to employ Sengru but feared that Shen and Deyu would obstruct this within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，出德裕為浙西觀察使，乃用僧孺為平章事，以紳為御史中丞，冀離內職，易掎摭而逐之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year Deyu was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Zhexi; Sengru was then employed as Associate Counselor and Shen as Vice Censor-in-Chief, hoping to remove him from inner duties and make it easier to seize on faults and drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year Deyu was sent out as observation commissioner of Zhexi; Sengru was then employed as associate counselor and Shen as vice censor-in-chief, hoping to remove him from inner duties and make it easier to seize on faults and drive him out.

sentences.zh: 乃以吏部侍郎韓愈為京兆尹，兼御史大夫，放臺參。

translations.literal: Han Yu, Vice Minister of Personnel, was appointed Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, with censorate attendance released.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, vice minister of personnel, was appointed metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and concurrently censor-in-chief, with censorate attendance released.

sentences.zh: 知紳剛褊，必與韓愈忿爭。

translations.literal: Knowing Shen's rigidity and narrowness, they were certain he would quarrel angrily with Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Shen's rigidity and narrowness, they were certain he would quarrel angrily with Han Yu.

sentences.zh: 制出，紳果移牒往來，論臺府事體。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, Shen indeed exchanged memorials back and forth, debating the protocol of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was issued, Shen indeed exchanged memorials back and forth, debating the protocol of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 而愈復性訐，言辭不遜，大喧物議，由是兩罷之。

translations.literal: Yet Yu was also contentious by nature and his words were insolent, causing great public clamor; because of this both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu was also contentious by nature and his words were insolent, causing great public clamor; because of this both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 愈改兵部侍郎，紳為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Yu was changed to Vice Minister of War and Shen became Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was changed to vice minister of war and Shen became observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 天子待紳素厚，不悟逢吉之嫁禍，為其心希外任，乃令中使就第宣勞，賜之玉帶。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had always treated Shen generously and did not perceive Fengji's scheme to shift blame; thinking Shen wished for an outer appointment, he sent a palace envoy to his residence to proclaim consolation and granted him a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always treated Shen generously and did not perceive Fengji's scheme to shift blame; thinking Shen wished for an outer appointment, he sent a palace envoy to his residence to proclaim consolation and granted him a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 紳對中使泣訴其事，言為逢吉所排，戀闕之情無已。

translations.literal: Shen wept before the palace envoy and explained the matter, saying he had been pushed aside by Fengji and his longing for the court was unending.
translations.idiomatic: Shen wept before the palace envoy and explained the matter, saying he had been pushed aside by Fengji and his longing for the court was unending.

sentences.zh: 及中謝日，面自陳訴，帝方省悟，乃改授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: On the day of his court thanks he personally stated his grievance; the emperor then came to understand and changed his appointment to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his court thanks he personally stated his grievance; the emperor then came to understand and changed his appointment to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 中尉王守澄用事，逢吉令門生故吏結托守澄為援以傾紳，晝夜計畫。

translations.literal: Chief Eunuch Wang Shoucheng held power; Fengji had his students and former subordinates cultivate Shoucheng as support to topple Shen, plotting day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng held power; Fengji had his students and former subordinates cultivate Shoucheng as support to topple Shen, plotting day and night.

sentences.zh: 會紳族子虞，文學知名，隱居華陽，自言不樂仕進，時來京師省紳。

translations.literal: It happened that Shen's clansman Yu, renowned in letters, lived in seclusion at Huayang, saying he took no joy in pursuing office, and from time to time came to the capital to visit Shen.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Shen's clansman Yu, renowned in letters, lived in seclusion at Huayang, saying he took no joy in pursuing office, and from time to time came to the capital to visit Shen.
