sentences.zh: 虞與從伯耆、進士程昔範，皆依紳。

translations.literal: Yu, together with his elder clansman Qi and jinshi Cheng Xifan, all relied on Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, together with his elder clansman Qi and jinshi Cheng Xifan, all relied on Shen.

sentences.zh: 及耆拜左拾遺，虞在華陽寓書與耆求薦，書誤達於紳。

translations.literal: When Qi was appointed Left Remonstrance Reminder, Yu from Huayang sent a letter to Qi requesting recommendation, and the letter mistakenly reached Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was appointed left remonstrance reminder, Yu from Huayang sent a letter to Qi requesting recommendation, and the letter mistakenly reached Shen.

sentences.zh: 紳以其進退二三，以書誚之。

translations.literal: Shen, because his going and coming was inconsistent, rebuked him in a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, because his going and coming was inconsistent, rebuked him in a letter.

sentences.zh: 虞大怨望。

translations.literal: Yu was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 及來京師，盡以紳嘗所密話言逢吉奸邪附會之語告逢吉。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital he told Fengji everything Shen had once said in confidence about Fengji's treachery and factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the capital he told Fengji everything Shen had once said in confidence about Fengji's treachery and factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 逢吉大怒，問計於門人張又新、李續之，咸曰：「搢紳皆自惜毛羽，孰肯為相公搏擊！

translations.literal: Fengji was greatly angered and asked his students Zhang Youxin and Li Xuzhi for a plan; all said: "Officials all cherish their own reputations—who would be willing to strike blows for the Chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was greatly angered and asked his students Zhang Youxin and Li Xuzhi for a plan; all said: "Officials all cherish their own reputations—who would be willing to strike blows for the chancellor!

sentences.zh: 須得非常奇士出死力者。

translations.literal: One must have an extraordinary man who will exert himself to the death.
translations.idiomatic: One must have an extraordinary man who will exert himself to the death.

sentences.zh: 有前鄧州司倉劉棲楚者，嘗為吏。

translations.literal: There was a former Warehouse Clerk of Deng Prefecture, Liu Qichu, who had once served as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: There was a former warehouse clerk of Deng Prefecture, Liu Qichu, who had once served as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王承宗以事繩之。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture bound him over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture bound him over an affair.

sentences.zh: 棲楚以首觸地固爭，而承宗竟不能奪，其果銳如此。

translations.literal: Qichu knocked his head on the ground and firmly resisted, and Chengzong in the end could not prevail—so resolute was he.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu kowtowed on the ground and firmly resisted, and Chengzong in the end could not prevail—so resolute was he.

sentences.zh: 若相公取之為諫官，令伺紳之失，一旦於上前暴揚其過，恩寵必替。

translations.literal: If the Chancellor takes him as remonstrating official and has him watch for Shen's faults, then one day before the emperor expose his errors—imperial favor will surely be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: If the chancellor takes him as remonstrating official and has him watch for Shen's faults, then one day before the emperor expose his errors—imperial favor will surely be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 事茍不行，過在棲楚，亦不足惜也。」

translations.literal: If the affair fails, the fault lies with Qichu and that is not worth regretting."
translations.idiomatic: If the affair fails, the fault lies with Qichu and that is not worth regretting.

sentences.zh: 逢吉乃用李虞、程昔範、劉棲楚，皆擢為拾遺，以伺紳隙。

translations.literal: Fengji then employed Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, and Liu Qichu, all promoted as remonstrance reminders, to watch for openings against Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji then employed Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, and Liu Qichu, all promoted as remonstrance reminders, to watch for openings against Shen.

sentences.zh: 俄而穆宗晏駕。

translations.literal: Soon Muzong passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Muzong passed away.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初即位，逢吉快紳失勢，慮嗣君復用之。

translations.literal: When Jingzong first took the throne, Fengji rejoiced at Shen's loss of power but feared the succeeding ruler would employ him again.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong first took the throne, Fengji rejoiced at Shen's loss of power but feared the succeeding ruler would employ him again.

sentences.zh: 張又新等謀逐紳。

translations.literal: Zhang Youxin and others plotted to drive Shen out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Youxin and others plotted to drive Shen out.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史蘇遇入朝，遇能決陰事，眾問計於遇。

translations.literal: It happened that Prefect of Jing Prefecture Su Yu entered court; Yu could resolve secret affairs, and the group asked him for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that prefect of Jing Prefecture Su Yu entered court; Yu could resolve secret affairs, and the group asked him for a plan.

sentences.zh: 遇曰：「上聽政後，當開延英，必有次對，官欲拔本塞源，先以次對為慮，余不足恃。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "After the emperor begins hearing government, the Yanying Hall will open and there will certainly be sequential audiences; if you wish to uproot the source, first worry about the sequential audiences—I am not enough to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "After the emperor begins hearing government, the Yanying Hall will open and there will certainly be sequential audiences; if you wish to uproot the source, first worry about the sequential audiences—I am not enough to rely on.

sentences.zh: 群黨深然之。

translations.literal: The faction deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The faction deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 逢吉乃以遇為左常侍。

translations.literal: Fengji then appointed Yu as Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji then appointed Yu as left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 王守澄每從容謂敬宗曰：「陛下登九五，逢吉之助也。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng often said casually to Jingzong: "Your Majesty's ascension to the throne was aided by Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng often said casually to Jingzong: "Your Majesty's ascension to the throne was aided by Fengji.

sentences.zh: 先朝初定儲貳，唯臣備知。

translations.literal: When the former court first fixed the heir apparent, I alone know fully.
translations.idiomatic: When the former court first fixed the heir apparent, I alone know fully.

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士杜元穎、李紳勸立深王，而逢吉固請立陛下，而李續之、李虞繼獻章疏。」

translations.literal: At that time Hanlin Academicians Du Yuanying and Li Shen urged establishing Prince Shen, while Fengji firmly requested establishing Your Majesty, and Li Xuzhi and Li Yu successively submitted memorials."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hanlin academicians Du Yuanying and Li Shen urged establishing Prince Shen, while Fengji firmly requested establishing Your Majesty, and Li Xuzhi and Li Yu successively submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝雖沖年，亦疑其事。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was young, he also doubted this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was young, he also doubted this matter.

sentences.zh: 會逢吉進擬，進李紳在內署時，嘗不利於陛下，請行貶逐。

translations.literal: When Fengji submitted nominations, he advanced that while Li Shen was in the inner offices he had once been unfavorable to Your Majesty and requested his demotion and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengji submitted nominations, he advanced that while Li Shen was in the inner offices he had once been unfavorable to Your Majesty and requested his demotion and banishment.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，方倚大臣，不能自執，乃貶紳端州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor had just taken the throne and was relying on senior ministers; unable to decide for himself, he demoted Shen to Army Vice Commander of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just taken the throne and was relying on senior ministers; unable to decide for himself, he demoted Shen to army vice commander of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貶制既行，百僚中書賀宰相，唯右拾遺吳思不賀。

translations.literal: Once the demotion edict was issued, the hundred officials submitted congratulations to the chancellor at the Secretariat—only Right Remonstrance Reminder Wu Si did not congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Once the demotion edict was issued, the hundred officials submitted congratulations to the chancellor at the secretariat—only right remonstrance reminder Wu Si did not congratulate.

sentences.zh: 逢吉怒，改為殿中侍御史，充入吐蕃告哀使。

translations.literal: Fengji was angered and changed him to Attending Palace Censor, assigned as envoy to Tibet to announce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was angered and changed him to attending palace censor, assigned as envoy to Tibet to announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 紳之貶也，正人腹誹，無敢有言。

translations.literal: At Shen's demotion, upright men murmured in their hearts but none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen's demotion, upright men murmured in their hearts but none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 唯翰林學士韋處厚上疏，極言逢吉奸邪，誣摭紳罪，語在《處厚傳》。

translations.literal: Only Hanlin Academician Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial forcefully declaring Fengji treacherous and falsely implicating Shen in crimes—the account is in the Biography of Chuhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou submitted a memorial forcefully declaring Fengji treacherous and falsely implicating Shen in crimes—the account is in the Biography of Chuhou.

sentences.zh: 天子亦稍開悟。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also gradually came to understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also gradually came to understand.

sentences.zh: 會禁中檢尋舊書，得穆宗時封書一篋。

translations.literal: When the inner palace searched old documents, a sealed box from Muzong's time was found.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner palace searched old documents, a sealed box from Muzong's time was found.

sentences.zh: 發之，得裴度、杜元穎與紳三人所獻疏，請立敬宗為太子。

translations.literal: Opening it, they found memorials submitted by Pei Du, Du Yuanying, and Shen—the three requesting that Jingzong be established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Opening it, they found memorials submitted by Pei Du, Du Yuanying, and Shen—the three requesting that Jingzong be established as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝感悟興嘆，悉命焚逢吉黨所上謗書，由是讒言稍息，紳黨得保全。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to sigh with understanding and ordered all slanderous documents submitted by Fengji's faction burned; thereby calumny gradually subsided and Shen's faction was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to sigh with understanding and ordered all slanderous documents submitted by Fengji's faction burned; thereby calumny gradually subsided and Shen's faction was preserved.

sentences.zh: 及寶歷改元大赦，逢吉定赦書節文，不欲紳量移，但雲左降官已經量移者與量移，不言左降官與量移。

translations.literal: When Baoli changed the era name and granted a great amnesty, Fengji drafted the amnesty text and did not wish Shen to be transferred closer; it only said that demoted officials already transferred closer would receive further transfer—not that demoted officials would receive transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoli changed the era name and granted a great amnesty, Fengji drafted the amnesty text and did not wish Shen to be transferred closer; it only said that demoted officials already transferred closer would receive further transfer—not that demoted officials would receive transfer.

sentences.zh: 韋處厚復上疏論之，語在《處厚傳》。

translations.literal: Wei Chuhou again submitted a memorial arguing the point—the account is in the Biography of Chuhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou again submitted a memorial arguing the point—the account is in the Biography of Chuhou.

sentences.zh: 帝特追赦書，添節文雲「左降官與量移」，紳方移為江州長史。

translations.literal: The emperor specially issued a follow-up amnesty adding the clause 'demoted officials receive transfer,' and Shen was then transferred to Chief Administrator of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially issued a follow-up amnesty adding the clause 'demoted officials receive transfer,' and Shen was then transferred to chief administrator of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to mentor of the heir apparent, with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，李德裕作相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe Li Deyu became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 7 Li Deyu became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 七月，檢校左常侍、越州刺史、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Yue Prefecture, and Observation Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed acting left regular attendant, prefect of Yue Prefecture, and observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 九年，李訓用事，李宗閔復相，與李訓、鄭註連衡排擯德裕罷相，紳與德裕俱以太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Li Xun held power; Li Zongmin again became chancellor and, together with Li Xun and Zheng Zhu in alliance, pushed aside Deyu and dismissed him as chancellor; Shen and Deyu both served as mentors of the heir apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Li Xun held power; Li Zongmin again became chancellor and, together with Li Xun and Zheng Zhu in alliance, pushed aside Deyu and dismissed him as chancellor; Shen and Deyu both served as mentors of the heir apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，加檢校尚書右僕射、揚州大都督府長史，知淮南節度大使事。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, Shen was further appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Yangzhou, and in charge of the Military Governorship of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, Shen was further appointed acting right vice director of the secretariat, chief administrator of the metropolitan prefecture of Yangzhou, and in charge of the military governorship of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年，入為兵部侍郎、同平章事，改中書侍郎，累遷守右僕射、門下侍郎、監修國史、上柱國、趙國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huichang, he entered court as Vice Minister of War and Associate Counselor, was changed to Vice Director in the Secretariat, and was successively advanced to Right Vice Director, Vice Director in the Chancellery, Supervisor of History Compilation, Senior Pillar of State, and Duke of Zhao, with an enfeoffment stipend of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 1 he entered court as vice minister of war and associate counselor, was made vice director in the secretariat, and rose through the ranks to right vice director, vice director in the chancellery, supervisor of history compilation, senior pillar of state, and duke of Zhao, with a stipend of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年，暴中風恙，足緩不任朝謁，拜章求罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he suddenly suffered a wind ailment; his feet were slow and he could not bear court audience, and he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he suddenly suffered a stroke; his legs grew weak and he could no longer attend court, so he submitted a memorial asking to resign.

sentences.zh: 十一月，守僕射、平章事，出為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he retained the titles Right Vice Director and Associate Counselor and went out as Military Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he kept his titles as right vice director and associate counselor while taking up the post of military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 紳始以文藝節操進用，受顧禁中。

translations.literal: Shen at first advanced through literary talent and moral integrity and received favor in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had risen through literary talent and moral integrity and enjoyed favor within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後為朋黨所擠，濱於禍患。

translations.literal: Later he was squeezed out by factional parties and stood on the brink of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Later factional rivals pushed him aside and he came to the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 賴正人匡救，得以功名始終。

translations.literal: Relying on upright men to rescue and correct, he was able to see his merit and name through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to upright men who stepped in to save him, he preserved his reputation and career to the end.

sentences.zh: 歿後，宣宗即位，李德裕失勢罷相，歸洛陽；

translations.literal: After his death, when Xuanzong took the throne, Li Deyu lost power and was dismissed as chancellor, returning to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: After Shen's death, when Xuanzong came to the throne, Li Deyu lost power, was removed as chancellor, and returned to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 而宗閔、嗣復之黨崔鉉、白敏中、令狐綯欲置德裕深罪。

translations.literal: But the faction of Zongmin and Sifu—Cui Xuan, Bai Minzhong, and Linghu Tao—wished to impose serious crimes on Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: But Cui Xuan, Bai Minzhong, and Linghu Tao, allies of Zongmin and Sifu, sought to implicate Deyu in grave offenses.

sentences.zh: 大中初，教人發紳鎮揚州時舊事，以傾德裕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong, they had men bring up old matters from when Shen governed Yangzhou, in order to topple Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong era they had men dredge up old incidents from Shen's tenure at Yangzhou to bring Deyu down.

sentences.zh: 初，會昌五年，揚州江都縣尉吳湘坐贓下獄，準法當死，具事上聞。

translations.literal: Initially, in the fifth year of Huichang, Wu Xiang, Assistant Magistrate of Jiangdu County in Yang Prefecture, was imprisoned for corruption; by law he deserved death, and the full case was reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 5, Wu Xiang, assistant magistrate of Jiangdu County in Yang Prefecture, was imprisoned on corruption charges; by law the offense carried the death penalty, and the full case was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諫官疑其冤，論之。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials doubted the injustice and argued the case.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials suspected a miscarriage of justice and spoke out on the matter.

sentences.zh: 遣御史崔元藻覆推，與揚州所奏多同，湘竟伏法。

translations.literal: The court sent Censor Cui Yuanzao to re-investigate; his findings largely matched Yangzhou's report, and Xiang was executed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched censor Cui Yuanzao to reinvestigate; his findings largely matched Yangzhou's report, and Xiang was executed.

sentences.zh: 及德裕罷相，群怨方構，湘兄進士汝納，詣闕訴冤，言紳在淮南恃德裕之勢，枉殺臣弟。

translations.literal: When Deyu was dismissed as chancellor, accumulated resentments were just forming; Xiang's elder brother, jinshi Ru'na, came to the palace to plead injustice, saying Shen in Huainan relied on Deyu's power to execute his younger brother unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu lost the chancellorship, long-smoldering grievances flared up; Xiang's elder brother Ru'na, a jinshi graduate, came to the palace to appeal for justice, claiming Shen had used Deyu's influence in Huainan to have his younger brother killed unjustly.

sentences.zh: 德裕既貶，紳亦追削三任官告。

translations.literal: Once Deyu was demoted, Shen also had certificates for three successive offices revoked posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu was demoted, Shen's credentials for three consecutive offices were also posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 吳汝納者，澧州人，故韶州刺史武陵兄之子。

translations.literal: Wu Ru'na was a man of Li Prefecture, son of the elder brother of the former Prefect of Shao Prefecture, Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ru'na was a native of Li Prefecture and the nephew of the former prefect of Shao, Wuling.

sentences.zh: 武陵進士登第，有史學，與劉軻並以史才直史館。

translations.literal: Wuling passed the jinshi examination, possessed historical learning, and together with Liu Ke was appointed directly to the History Office for their talent in history.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling passed the jinshi examination, was versed in historiography, and alongside Liu Ke was appointed directly to the History Office for his historical expertise.

sentences.zh: 武陵撰《十三代史駁議》二十卷。

translations.literal: Wuling compiled twenty juan of "Critical Discussions on Thirteen Dynasties of History."
translations.idiomatic: Wuling compiled a twenty-juan work titled Critical Discussions on Thirteen Dynasties of History.

sentences.zh: 自尚書員外郎出為忠州刺史，改韶州。

translations.literal: From Assistant Director in a ministry he went out as Prefect of Zhong Prefecture, then was transferred to Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as an assistant director in a ministry, he was posted as prefect of Zhong Prefecture and later transferred to Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐贓貶潘州司戶卒。

translations.literal: For corruption he was demoted to Registrar of Pan Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of corruption, he was demoted to registrar of Pan Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 汝納亦進士擢第，以季父贓罪，久之不調。

translations.literal: Ru'na also passed the jinshi examination; because of his uncle's corruption conviction, he went long without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ru'na also passed the jinshi examination, but because of his uncle's corruption conviction he went for years without receiving an appointment.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，為河南府永寧縣尉。

translations.literal: During Huichang he served as Assistant Magistrate of Yongning County in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era he served as assistant magistrate of Yongning County in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，武陵坐贓時，李德裕作相，貶之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wuling was convicted of corruption, Li Deyu was chancellor and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wuling was convicted of corruption, Li Deyu was serving as chancellor and had him demoted.

sentences.zh: 故汝納以不調挾怨，而附宗閔、嗣復之黨，同作謗言。

translations.literal: Therefore Ru'na, nursing resentment over his lack of appointment, joined the faction of Zongmin and Sifu and together spread slander.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a grudge over his stalled career, Ru'na joined the faction of Zongmin and Sifu and helped spread slanderous accusations.

sentences.zh: 會汝納弟湘為江都尉，為部人所訟贓罪，兼娶百姓顏悅女為妻，有逾格律。

translations.literal: It happened that Ru'na's younger brother Xiang was assistant magistrate of Jiangdu and was accused by subordinates of corruption; he had also taken a commoner's daughter, Yan Yue, as wife, in violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ru'na's younger brother Xiang, then assistant magistrate of Jiangdu, was denounced by subordinates for corruption and had also married a commoner's daughter, Yan Yue, in violation of the regulations.

sentences.zh: 李紳令觀察判官魏铏鞫之，贓狀明白，伏法。

translations.literal: Li Shen had Observation Commissioner's aide Wei Xing interrogate the case; the corruption was clearly established, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen had the observation commissioner's aide Wei Xing investigate; the corruption was clearly established, and Xiang was executed.

sentences.zh: 湘妻顏，顏繼母焦，皆笞而釋之。

translations.literal: Xiang's wife Yan and Yan's stepmother Jiao were both flogged and released.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's wife Yan and Yan's stepmother Jiao were both flogged and then released.

sentences.zh: 仍令江都令張弘思以船監送湘妻顏及兒女送澧州。

translations.literal: Shen also ordered Magistrate of Jiangdu Zhang Hongsi to escort by boat under guard Xiang's wife Yan and her children to Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen also ordered the magistrate of Jiangdu, Zhang Hongsi, to escort Xiang's wife Yan and her children by boat under guard to Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及揚州上具獄，物議以德裕素憎吳氏，疑李紳織成其罪。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou submitted the complete case, public opinion held that Deyu had always hated the Wu clan and suspected Li Shen of fabricating the crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou submitted the complete dossier, public opinion held that Deyu had long despised the Wu family and suspected Li Shen of having fabricated the charges.

sentences.zh: 諫官論之，乃差御史崔元藻為制使，覆吳湘獄，

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials argued the case, and Censor Cui Yuanzao was dispatched as imperial commissioner to reinvestigate the Wu Xiang case.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials raised objections, and censor Cui Yuanzao was dispatched as imperial commissioner to reinvestigate the Wu Xiang case.

sentences.zh: 據款伏妄破程糧錢，計贓準法。

translations.literal: According to the confession, he had falsely depleted travel-ration funds; calculating the stolen goods by law,
translations.idiomatic: According to the confession, Xiang had improperly depleted travel-ration funds; when the theft was calculated under the law,

sentences.zh: 其恃官娶百姓顏悅女為妻，則稱悅是前青州衙推。

translations.literal: as for his taking advantage of office to marry the commoner Yan Yue's daughter as wife, it was claimed that Yue had been a former yamen secretary of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: regarding his abuse of office in marrying the commoner Yan Yue's daughter, it was claimed that Yue had formerly served as a yamen secretary in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 悅先娶王氏，是衣冠女，非繼室焦所生，與揚州案小有不同。

translations.literal: Yue had first married a woman surnamed Wang, who was a woman of the gentry and not born of the stepmother Jiao; this differed slightly from the Yangzhou case.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's first wife had been a woman of the Wang clan, a lady of good family and not a daughter of the stepmother Jiao—a point that differed slightly from the Yangzhou findings.

sentences.zh: 德裕以元藻無定奪，奏貶崖州司戶。

translations.literal: Deyu, because Yuanzao had made no definitive ruling, memorialized to demote him to Registrar of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuanzao had failed to reach a definitive ruling, Deyu memorialized to have him demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及汝納進狀，追元藻覆問。

translations.literal: When Ru'na submitted his petition, Yuanzao was pursued and recalled for renewed questioning.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru'na submitted his petition, Yuanzao was recalled to court for further questioning.

sentences.zh: 元藻既恨德裕，陰為崔鉉、白敏中、令狐綯所利誘，即言湘雖坐贓，罪不至死。

translations.literal: Yuanzao, already resentful of Deyu, was secretly enticed by Cui Xuan, Bai Minzhong, and Linghu Tao and then declared that although Xiang had been convicted of corruption, the crime did not warrant death.
translations.idiomatic: Already resentful of Deyu, Yuanzao was secretly won over by Cui Xuan, Bai Minzhong, and Linghu Tao and then testified that although Xiang had been guilty of corruption, the offense did not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 又雲，顏悅實非百姓，此獄是鄭亞首唱，元壽協李恪鍛成，李回便奏。

translations.literal: He also said that Yan Yue was in fact not a commoner, that Zheng Ya had initiated this case, Yuan Shou had assisted Li Ke in forging it, and Li Hui had promptly memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed that Yan Yue was not truly a commoner, that Zheng Ya had instigated the case, Yuan Shou had helped Li Ke fabricate it, and Li Hui had promptly memorialized the findings.

sentences.zh: 遂下三司詳鞫。

translations.literal: The case was then referred to the Three Offices for detailed interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The case was then referred to the Three Offices for a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 故德裕再貶，李回、鄭亞等皆竄逐。

translations.literal: Therefore Deyu was demoted again, and Li Hui, Zheng Ya, and others were all banished.
translations.idiomatic: As a result Deyu was demoted again, and Li Hui, Zheng Ya, and others were all banished.

sentences.zh: 吳汝納、崔元藻為崔、白、令狐所獎，數年並至顯官。

translations.literal: Wu Ru'na and Cui Yuanzao were rewarded by Cui, Bai, and Linghu, and within several years both reached prominent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ru'na and Cui Yuanzao were rewarded by Cui, Bai, and Linghu, and within a few years both rose to prominent offices.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年，劉稹據潞州，邀求旄鉞，朝議不允，加兵問罪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huichang, Liu Zhen held Lu Prefecture and demanded a military commission; court deliberation did not grant it, and troops were added to question him by force.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang 3, Liu Zhen seized Lu Prefecture and demanded a military commission; the court refused, and an expedition was launched against him.

sentences.zh: 武宗懼稹陰附河朔三鎮，以沮王師，乃命回奉使河朔。

translations.literal: Wuzong feared Zhen would secretly attach himself to the three Hebei circuits and obstruct the imperial army, and therefore ordered Hui on an embassy to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong feared Zhen might secretly align with the three Hebei circuits and thwart the imperial campaign, so he dispatched Hui on an embassy to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 魏博何弘敬、鎮冀王元逵皆具櫜鞬郊迎。

translations.literal: He Jing of Weibo and Wang Yuankui of Zhenji both came to the suburbs bearing bow cases and quivers to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He Jing of Weibo and Wang Yuankui of Zhenji both rode out to the suburbs with bow cases and quivers to greet him.

sentences.zh: 回喻以朝旨，言澤潞密邇王畿，不同河北，自艱難已來，唯魏、鎮兩籓，列聖皆許襲，而稹無功，欲效河朔故事，理即太悖。

translations.literal: Hui explained the court's intent, saying Ze-Lu lay close to the imperial domain and was not like Hebei; since the times of hardship, only the two circuits of Wei and Zhen had been permitted hereditary succession by successive emperors, whereas Zhen had no merit yet wished to follow the Hebei precedent—the principle was utterly perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Hui explained the court's intent: Ze-Lu lay close to the capital region and was not comparable to Hebei; since the troubled times, only the Wei and Zhen circuits had been granted hereditary succession by successive emperors, yet Zhen, without merit, sought to follow the Hebei precedent—an utterly perverse claim.

sentences.zh: 聖上但以山東三郡，境連魏、鎮，用軍便近，王師不欲輕出山東，請魏、鎮兩籓只收山東三郡。

translations.literal: His Majesty only asks that because the three commanderies of Shandong border Wei and Zhen and deployment is convenient, the imperial army does not wish lightly to leave Shandong; he requests that the two circuits of Wei and Zhen take only the three Shandong commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked only that, because the three Shandong commanderies bordered Wei and Zhen and troops could be deployed conveniently from there, the imperial army need not march out of Shandong lightly; the Wei and Zhen circuits should take the three Shandong commanderies alone.

sentences.zh: 弘敬、元逵俯僂從命。

translations.literal: Jing and Yuankui bowed low and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yuankui bowed low and accepted the order.

sentences.zh: 幽州張仲武與太原劉沔攻回鶻。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongwu of You Prefecture and Liu Mian of Taiyuan attacked the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongwu of You Prefecture and Liu Mian of Taiyuan were campaigning against the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 時兩人不協，朝廷方用兵，不欲籓帥不和。

translations.literal: At the time the two men were not in accord; the court was just then using troops and did not wish the frontier commanders to be at odds.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two commanders were at odds; with the court already at war, it did not want discord among the frontier governors.

sentences.zh: 回至幽州，喻以和協之旨，仲武欣然釋憾。

translations.literal: When Hui reached You Prefecture, he explained the intent of reconciliation, and Zhongwu gladly released his resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached You Prefecture, he conveyed the court's call for cooperation, and Zhongwu gladly set aside his grievance.

sentences.zh: 乃移劉沔鎮滑臺，命仲武領太原軍攻潞。

translations.literal: Liu Mian was then transferred to garrison Huatai, and Zhongwu was ordered to lead the Taiyuan army to attack Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was transferred to Huatai, and Zhongwu was ordered to lead the Taiyuan army against Lu.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以本官同平章事，累加中書侍郎，轉門下，歷戶、吏二尚書。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he retained his original office as Associate Counselor, was successively promoted to Vice Director in the Secretariat, transferred to the Chancellery, and served as Minister of Revenue and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he retained his post as associate counselor, rose to vice director in the secretariat, moved to the chancellery, and served as minister of revenue and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 武宗崩，回充山陵使，祔廟竟，出為成都尹、劍南西川節度。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, Hui served as director of the imperial tomb; once the ancestral temple rites were complete, he went out as Prefect of Chengdu and Military Governor of Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, Hui served as director of the imperial tomb; once the ancestral rites were complete, he was posted as prefect of Chengdu and military governor of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 大中元年冬，坐與李德裕親善，改潭州刺史、湖南觀察使，再貶撫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Dazhong, for being close to Li Deyu he was changed to Prefect of Tan Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of Hunan, then demoted again to Prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Dazhong 1, because of his closeness to Li Deyu he was transferred to prefect of Tan and observation commissioner of Hunan, then demoted again to prefect of Fu.

sentences.zh: 白敏中、令狐綯罷相，入朝為兵部尚書，復出為成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: When Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao were dismissed as chancellors, he entered court as Minister of War, then went out again as Prefect of Chengdu and Military Governor of Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao left the chancellorship, he returned to court as minister of war, then was posted again as prefect of Chengdu and military governor of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister over the Masses, with the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted minister over the masses, with the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 李玨，字待價，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Jue, styled Daojia, was a man of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue, whose style was Daojia, was a native of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父仲朝。

translations.literal: His father: Zhongchao.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Zhongchao.

sentences.zh: 玨進士擢弟，又登書判拔萃科，累官至右拾遺。

translations.literal: Jue passed the jinshi examination, also passed the Outstanding in Document Analysis examination, and successively reached Right Remonstrance Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Jue passed the jinshi examination and also the Outstanding in Document Analysis examination, eventually rising to right remonstrance reminder.

sentences.zh: 穆宗荒於酒色，才終易月之制，即與勛臣飲宴。

translations.literal: Muzong was dissolute in wine and women; as soon as the abbreviated mourning period ended, he feasted and drank with meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong indulged in wine and women; scarcely had the abbreviated mourning period ended when he began feasting with his meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 玨與同列上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: Jue together with his colleagues submitted a memorial discussing this, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jue and his colleagues submitted a memorial arguing as follows:

sentences.zh: 臣聞人臣之節，本於忠盡，茍有所見，即宜上陳。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that a minister's integrity is rooted in loyal fulfillment; if one has a view, one should report it upward.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that a minister's duty is rooted in loyal service; whenever one sees something amiss, one should speak up.

sentences.zh: 況為陛下諫官，食陛下厚祿，豈敢腹誹巷議，辜負恩榮？

translations.literal: Moreover, as remonstrating officials for Your Majesty, eating Your Majesty's generous salary, how dare we murmur in our hearts or gossip in the lanes and fail our grace and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as Your Majesty's remonstrating officials, enjoying Your Majesty's generous salary, how could we grumble in private or gossip in the streets and betray that honor?

sentences.zh: 臣等聞諸道路，不知信否，皆云有詔追李光顏、李醖，欲於重陽節日，合宴群臣。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard on the roads, not knowing whether it is true, that there is an edict recalling Li Guangyan and Li Yun, intending on the Double Ninth Festival to hold a combined banquet for the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard along the roads—we do not know whether it is true—that an edict has recalled Li Guangyan and Li Yun for a combined banquet of the assembled ministers on the Double Ninth Festival.

sentences.zh: 倘誠有之，乃陛下念群臣，敷惠澤之慈旨也。

translations.literal: If this is indeed so, it is Your Majesty's kindly intent to think of the assembled ministers and spread gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: If this is indeed so, it reflects Your Majesty's kindly intent to remember the assembled ministers and bestow gracious favor.

sentences.zh: 然元朔未改，園陵尚新。

translations.literal: Yet the era name has not been changed and the imperial tombs are still new.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the era name has not been changed and the imperial tombs are still fresh.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下執易月之期，俯從人欲；

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty holds to the abbreviated mourning period and bows to human desire,
translations.idiomatic: Although Your Majesty has shortened the mourning period in deference to public sentiment,

sentences.zh: 而禮經著三年之制，猶服心喪。

translations.literal: the Ritual Classics prescribe three years of mourning, and one still wears mourning in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: the Ritual Classics prescribe three years of mourning, and one still observes mourning in the heart.

sentences.zh: 今遵同軌之會，適去於中邦；

translations.literal: now the assembly of unified mourning has only just departed from the central realm;
translations.idiomatic: Now the assembly for unified mourning has only just concluded in the capital;

sentences.zh: 告遠夷之使，未復其來命。

translations.literal: the envoys announcing to distant barbarians have not yet returned with their replies.
translations.idiomatic: the envoys sent to announce the mourning to distant peoples have not yet returned with their replies.

sentences.zh: 遏密弛禁，蓋為齊人，合宴內廷，事將未可。

translations.literal: Relaxing the prohibition on music was for the people of Qi; a combined banquet in the inner court is a matter that for the moment cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Relaxing the prohibition on music was meant for the people of Qi; holding a combined banquet in the inner court is something that cannot yet be done.

sentences.zh: 夫明王之舉動，為天下法；

translations.literal: The actions of an enlightened king are the standard for all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The actions of an enlightened ruler set the standard for all under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 王言既降，其出如綸。

translations.literal: once royal words descend, their going forth is like spun silk.
translations.idiomatic: once imperial words are issued, they go forth like binding decree.

sentences.zh: 茍玷皇猷，徒章直諫，臣等是以昧死上聞。

translations.literal: If they stain the imperial plan, remonstrance would be in vain; your subjects therefore risk death to report this.
translations.idiomatic: If they tarnish the imperial design, our remonstrance would be pointless; we therefore risk death to bring this to Your Majesty's attention.

sentences.zh: 且光顏、李愬，久立忠勞，今方盛秋，務拓邊境。

translations.literal: Moreover Guangyan and Li Su have long established loyal service; now at the height of autumn they are busy expanding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guangyan and Li Su have long rendered loyal service; now, at the height of autumn, they are busy expanding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如或召見，詔以謀猷，褒其宿勛，付以疆事，則與歌鐘合宴，酒食邀歡，不得同年而語也。

translations.literal: If they were summoned and issued an edict with strategy, praised for longstanding merit, and entrusted with frontier affairs—that cannot be spoken of in the same breath as summoning them to a banquet of bells and songs with wine and food for convivial pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: If they were summoned to discuss strategy, praised for their long service, and entrusted with frontier affairs—that is not to be compared with summoning them to a convivial banquet of music, wine, and feasting.

sentences.zh: 陛下自纘嗣以來，發號施令，無非孝理因心，形於詔敕，固以感動於人倫。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, in issuing orders and commands there has been nothing that was not filial governance arising from the heart, taking form in edicts and proclamations—this has indeed moved human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, every order and edict has sprung from filial governance of the heart and has indeed moved the hearts of men.

sentences.zh: 更在敬慎威儀，保持聖德而已。

translations.literal: What remains is reverent caution in bearing and demeanor and preserving sagely virtue—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: What remains is to maintain reverent caution in conduct and preserve sagely virtue—that is all.

sentences.zh: 上雖不用其言，慰勞遣之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor did not adopt their words, he consoled and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor did not accept their advice, he consoled them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，鹽鐵使王播增茶稅，初稅一百，增之五十，玨上疏論之曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Salt and Iron Commissioner Wang Bo increased the tea tax from an initial levy of one hundred to an added fifty; Jue submitted a memorial arguing as follows:
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 1, salt and iron commissioner Wang Bo raised the tea tax from one hundred to one hundred fifty; Jue submitted a memorial arguing as follows:

sentences.zh: 榷率救弊，起自干戈，天下無事，即宜蠲省。

translations.literal: Monopoly rates to remedy abuses arose from warfare; when all under Heaven is at peace, they should be reduced and eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly taxes to remedy fiscal abuses arose from wartime necessity; with the realm at peace, they should be reduced and abolished.

sentences.zh: 況稅茶之事，尤出近年，在貞元元年中，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Moreover the matter of taxing tea arose especially in recent years; in the first year of Zhenyuan it could not be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the tea tax is a recent innovation; in Zhenyuan 1 there was no alternative.

sentences.zh: 今四海鏡清，八方砥平，厚斂於人，殊傷國體。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are clear as a mirror and the eight directions level as a whetstone; heavy exactions upon the people greatly harm the body politic.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and the empire is settled; heavy exactions upon the people gravely harm the state.

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first reason it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 茶為食物，無異米鹽，於人所資，遠近同俗。

translations.literal: Tea is a foodstuff, no different from rice and salt; in what people rely on, near and far share the same custom.
translations.idiomatic: Tea is a staple of daily life, no different from rice or salt; people everywhere rely on it equally.

sentences.zh: 既袪竭乏，難舍斯須，田閭之間，嗜好尤切。

translations.literal: Once it relieves exhaustion it is hard to set aside even for a moment; among village fields the craving is especially keen.
translations.idiomatic: It relieves fatigue and is hard to do without even for a moment; in the countryside the craving is especially strong.

sentences.zh: 今增稅既重，時估必增，流弊於民，先及貧弱。

translations.literal: Now that the increased tax is heavy, market prices will surely rise; the harm flowing to the people will first reach the poor and weak.
translations.idiomatic: With the tax increase, market prices will surely rise, and the burden will fall first on the poor and weak.

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second reason it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 且山澤之饒，出無定數，量斤論稅，所冀售多。

translations.literal: Moreover the bounty of mountains and marshes has no fixed output; taxing by weight in jin is done in hope of greater sales.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the yield of mountains and marshes is unpredictable; taxing by weight is meant to encourage greater sales.

sentences.zh: 價高則市者稀，價賤則市者廣，歲終上計，其利幾何？

translations.literal: When prices are high buyers are few; when prices are low buyers are many—at year's end when accounts are submitted, how much profit will there be?
translations.idiomatic: When prices are high, buyers are scarce; when prices are low, buyers are plentiful—when the year-end accounts are tallied, how much profit will there actually be?

sentences.zh: 未見阜財，徒聞斂怨。

translations.literal: One does not see enriched revenue; one only hears accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury sees no enrichment; one hears only growing public resentment.

sentences.zh: 其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third reason it should not be done.

sentences.zh: 時禁中造百尺樓，國計不充。

translations.literal: At that time within the forbidden palace a hundred-foot tower was being built, and state revenue was not sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the inner palace was constructing a hundred-foot tower, and the treasury could not cover the cost.

sentences.zh: 王播希恩增稅，奉帝嗜欲，疏奏不省。

translations.literal: Wang Bo, seeking favor, increased the tax to gratify the emperor's desires; the memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo, seeking imperial favor, raised the tax to indulge the emperor's desires; the memorial went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部員外郎，轉司勛員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Jue was transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Honors with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Jue was promoted to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel, then to assistant director in the Ministry of Honors with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，文宗謂宰臣曰：「朕在位十四年，屬天下無事，雖未至理，亦少有如今日之無事也。」

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, Wenzong said to the chancellors: "I have been on the throne fourteen years; it has happened that all under Heaven is at peace; although we have not reached perfect order, there have rarely been days as untroubled as today."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, Wenzong said to the chancellors: "I have reigned for fourteen years, and the realm has been at peace; though we have not reached perfect order, rarely have times been as untroubled as today."

sentences.zh: 玨對曰：「邦國安危，亦知人之身。

translations.literal: Jue replied: "The safety or danger of the state is like the body of a person.
translations.idiomatic: Jue replied: "The safety or danger of the state is like the health of a person.

sentences.zh: 當四體和平之時，長宜調適，以順寒暄之節。

translations.literal: When the four limbs are in harmony, one should long regulate and adjust to follow the alternation of cold and warm seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When the body is in harmony, one should continually adjust to follow the changing seasons.

sentences.zh: 如恃安自忽，則疾患旋生。

translations.literal: If one relies on peace and neglects oneself, illness will quickly arise.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes peace for granted and grows careless, illness will soon follow.

sentences.zh: 朝廷當無事之時，思省闕失而補之，則禍難不作矣。」

translations.literal: When the court is at peace, one should reflect on omissions and failures and remedy them—then calamity will not arise."
translations.idiomatic: When the court enjoys peace, it should reflect on its shortcomings and remedy them—then disaster will not arise."

sentences.zh: 文宗以杜悰領度支稱職，欲加戶部尚書，因紫宸言之。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because Du Cong was competent in charge of the Directorate of Revenue, wished to add the title Minister of Revenue and spoke of it at the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, finding Du Cong competent as director of revenue, wished to promote him to minister of revenue and raised the matter at the Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 陳夷行曰：「一切恩權，合歸君上。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing said: "All favors and authority ought to belong to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing said: "Every grant of favor and every exercise of power should rest with Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 陛下自看可否？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty yourself should see whether each matter is acceptable or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty judge each proposal on its merits."

sentences.zh: 玨對曰：「太宗用宰臣，天下事皆先平章，謂之平章事。

translations.literal: Jue replied: "When Emperor Taizong employed chancellors, all affairs under Heaven were first deliberated with the pingzhang—hence the office called Pingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue replied: "When Emperor Taizong relied on his chancellors, state business was first settled through joint deliberation—the origin of the title Grand Councillor, or Pingzhangshi.

sentences.zh: 代天理物，上下無疑，所以致太平者也。

translations.literal: They assisted Heaven in governing things; above and below were without doubt—this is how peace was brought about.
translations.idiomatic: They stood in for Heaven in ordering the realm, so that ruler and subjects had no doubts— that is how peace was achieved.

sentences.zh: 若拜一官，命一職，事事皆決於君上，即焉用彼相？

translations.literal: If for every appointment of an office and assignment of a post every matter is decided by the sovereign, then of what use are those chancellors?
translations.idiomatic: If every appointment and every decision rests solely with the throne, what need is there for chancellors at all?

sentences.zh: 昔隋文帝一切自勞心力，臣下發論則疑，凡臣下用之則宰相，不用是常僚，豈可自保？

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Sui personally toiled over everything in his mind; when subordinates offered counsel he grew suspicious. Whenever he used a subordinate that man became chancellor; if not used he remained an ordinary official—how could one protect himself?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui once exhausted himself micromanaging every affair: he doubted ministers who spoke up, elevated anyone he happened to employ to chancellor, and left the rest as ordinary officials—under such conditions, who could feel secure in office?

sentences.zh: 陛下常語臣云：『竇易直勸我，宰相進擬，但五人留三人、兩人，勾一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty often told me: 'Dou Yizhi advised me that when chancellors submit nominations, I need only keep three or two of five and cross out one.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once told me: 'Dou Yizhi urged that when chancellors put forward candidates, I should keep three or two from a list of five and strike one name off.

sentences.zh: 渠即合勸我擇宰相，不合勸我疑宰相。』」

translations.literal: He ought to have advised me to choose chancellors, not advised me to distrust chancellors.'
translations.idiomatic: His duty was to help me select good chancellors, not to teach me to suspect the chancellors I already have.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「易直此言甚鄙。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Dou Yizhi's words on this are quite base."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What Dou Yizhi said was contemptibly small-minded."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「韋處厚作相，三日薦六度師，亦大可怪。」

translations.literal: He added: "When Wei Chuhou served as chancellor, within three days he recommended Liudushi—that too was greatly strange."
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "When Wei Chuhou became chancellor, he recommended the monk Liudushi within three days—that was equally astonishing."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「處厚淫於奉佛，不悟其是非也。」

translations.literal: Jue said: "Chuhou was excessive in his devotion to Buddhism and did not discern right from wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue said: "Chuhou was so absorbed in Buddhist observance that he lost sight of what was proper."

sentences.zh: 其年五月，上謂宰臣曰：「貞元政事，初年至好。」

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month, the emperor said to the chancellors: "The Zhenyuan administration was at its best in the early years."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year the emperor told his chancellors: "Government under the Zhenyuan reign started out well."

sentences.zh: 玨曰：「德宗中年好貨，方鎮進奉，即加恩澤。

translations.literal: Jue said: "In mid-reign Emperor Dezong came to love wealth; when regional commanders presented tribute, he at once granted them favors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue replied: "In his middle years Emperor Dezong grew greedy; whenever a regional commander sent tribute, he showered him with rewards.

sentences.zh: 租賦出自百姓，更令貪吏剝削，聚貨以希恩，理道故不可也。」

translations.literal: Rent and tax come from the common people; greedy officials were further allowed to strip them, amassing goods to seek favor—thus the Way of governance could not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Taxes are drawn from the people, yet corrupt officials were allowed to squeeze them further, hoarding wealth to curry favor—such a course could never sustain good government."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人君聚斂，猶自不可。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For the ruler himself to amass wealth is already unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Even when the ruler himself hoards revenue, that is already wrong.

sentences.zh: 但輕賦節用可也。」

translations.literal: Only light taxation and restrained spending will do."
translations.idiomatic: Lightening burdens and practicing frugality is enough."

sentences.zh: 玨又曰：「貞觀中，房、杜、王、魏啟告文皇，意只在此，請不易初心。

translations.literal: Jue also said: "In the Zhenguan era, Fang, Du, Wang, and Wei opened counsel to Emperor Wen and advised him with intent only here—please do not change your original resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue added: "During Zhenguan, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Wang Gui, and Wei Zheng urged Emperor Taizong along these very lines—I beg Your Majesty not to abandon that first intention.

sentences.zh: 自古好事，克終實難。」

translations.literal: From antiquity, good undertakings are in truth hard to carry through to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, it has been difficult to see a worthy project through to the finish."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕心終不改也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My heart will in the end not change."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "My resolve will never waver."

sentences.zh: 尋封贊皇男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zanhuang, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Jue was created Baron of Zanhuang with an estate of three hundred tax households.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位之年九月，與楊嗣復俱罷相，出為桂州刺史、桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the year Wuzong ascended the throne, he and Yang Sifu were both removed as chancellors and sent out as Governor of Gui Prefecture and Gui-Guan Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the year Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Jue and Yang Sifu were both dismissed from the chancellorship and appointed Governor of Gui Prefecture and Observation Commissioner of the Gui circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年，長流驩州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was permanently exiled to Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was banished to distant Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，崔鉉、白敏中逐李德裕，征入朝為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong, Cui Xuan and Bai Minzhong drove out Li Deyu; Jue was summoned to court as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dazhong era, after Cui Xuan and Bai Minzhong ousted Li Deyu, Jue was recalled to the capital as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 出為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，累遷金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射、揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度使、上柱國、贊皇郡開國公、食邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: He entered as Minister of Personnel and was promoted in succession to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, Inspector-General and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, Military Governor of Huainan, Supporter of the State, Duke of Zanhuang Commandery with a founding fief, and a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as minister of personnel and rose through a string of honors: grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal, acting right vice director of the secretariat, chief administrator of Yangzhou, military governor of Huainan, supporter of the state, and founding Duke of Zanhuang with fifteen hundred tax households.

sentences.zh: 大中七年卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong he died and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Dazhong and was posthumously created minister of works.

sentences.zh: 李固言，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Guyan was a man of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guyan was a native of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖並，父現。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Bing; his father was Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Li Bing and his father Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 固言，元和七年登進士甲科。

translations.literal: Guyan, in the seventh year of Yuanhe, passed the jinshi examination in the first class.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanhe, Guyan passed the jinshi examination with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 太和初，累官至賀部郎中、知臺雜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he rose in succession to Director in the He Bureau and handled miscellaneous censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taihe period he advanced to bureau director in the ministry of personnel and took charge of miscellaneous censorate business.

sentences.zh: 四年，李宗閔作相，用為給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Li Zongmin became chancellor, Guyan was appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Li Zongmin, upon becoming chancellor, appointed him supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 五年，宋申錫為王守澄誣陷，固言與同列伏閣論之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Song Shenxi was falsely implicated by Wang Shoucheng; Guyan and his colleagues prostrated themselves in the corridor to remonstrate on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Song Shenxi was framed by Wang Shoucheng, Guyan and his fellow officials lay prostrate in the palace corridor to protest the injustice.

sentences.zh: 將作監王堪修奉太廟弛慢，罰俸，仍改官為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Wang Kan, Director of Palace Construction, was negligent in maintaining the Imperial Ancestral Temple; his salary was fined and his post was changed to Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan, director of palace construction, was punished with a salary fine and reassigned from his negligent care of the ancestral temple to the post of preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 制出，固言封還曰：「東宮調護之地，不可令弛慢被罰之人處之。」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Guyan returned it sealed and said: "The Eastern Palace is a place for nurturing and protecting the heir—one cannot place there a man who was negligent and punished."
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict appeared, Guyan sealed it and sent it back, saying: "The heir's household is where the future ruler is formed; it is no place for an official already censured for negligence.

sentences.zh: 改為均王傅。

translations.literal: The appointment was changed to Tutor of the Prince of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The order was revised to make him tutor to the Prince of Jun instead.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 七年四月，轉尚書左丞，奉詔定左右僕射上事儀註。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year he was moved to Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat and received an edict to fix the protocol for the left and right vice directors when they attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year he became left assistant director of the secretariat and was ordered to draft the ceremonial regulations governing the left and right vice directors in office.

sentences.zh: 八年，李德裕輔政，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Li Deyu assisted in government, Guyan was sent out as Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Li Deyu took power, Guyan was posted as governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，宗閔復入，召拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Zongmin returned to power; Guyan was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That October, when Zongmin returned to court, Guyan was recalled and made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年五月，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year he was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 六月，宗閔得罪，固言代為門下侍郎、平章事，尋加崇文館大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zongmin fell from favor; Guyan replaced him as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor, and soon was added as Grand Academician of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, after Zongmin's disgrace, Guyan succeeded him as vice director of the chancellery and grand councillor, and was soon made grand academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 時李訓、鄭註用事，自欲竊輔相之權。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu held power and wished themselves to steal the authority of the assisting chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Zheng Zhu were then in control and sought to seize the chancellors' power for themselves.

sentences.zh: 宗閔既逐，外示公體，爰立固言，其實惡與宗閔朋黨。

translations.literal: Once Zongmin was driven out, outwardly they displayed public rectitude in raising Guyan, but in truth they hated his factional tie with Zongmin.
translations.idiomatic: With Zongmin gone, they installed Guyan as a show of impartiality, though in fact they resented his association with Zongmin's faction.

sentences.zh: 九月，以兵部尚書出為興元節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was sent out as Military Governor of Xingyuan with the title Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he left the capital as minister of war and military governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 李訓自代固言為平章事。

translations.literal: Li Xun himself replaced Guyan as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun took Guyan's place as grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 訓、註誅，文宗思其讜正，開成元年四月，復召為平章事，判戶部事。

translations.literal: After Xun and Zhu were executed, Wenzong recalled Guyan's forthright rectitude; in the fourth month of the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Grand Councillor with charge of Ministry of Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun and Zhu were put to death, Emperor Wenzong remembered Guyan's honest counsel; in the fourth month of the first year of Kaicheng he was recalled as grand councillor with concurrent charge of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，君臣上徽號，上紫宸言曰：「中外上章，請加徽號。

translations.literal: In the second year, ruler and ministers submitted an honorific title; at the Zichen Hall the emperor spoke: "Within and without, memorials have asked that an honorific be added.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year court and throne jointly proposed an honorific epithet; at the Zichen Hall the emperor said: "Officials throughout the empire have petitioned to add an honorific to my title.

sentences.zh: 朕思理道猶郁，實愧嶽牧之請。

translations.literal: I consider that the Way of governance is still obstructed and am truly ashamed before the request of the regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I feel that good government is still blocked, and I am ashamed to accept this request from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 如聞州郡甚有無政處？」

translations.literal: As I have heard, are there not many places in the prefectures and districts where there is no good administration?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that many prefectures and districts are badly governed—is that so?"

sentences.zh: 固言曰：「人言鄧州王堪衰老，隋州鄭襄無政。」

translations.literal: Guyan said: "People say Wang Kan of Deng Prefecture is aged and feeble, and Zheng Xiang of Sui Prefecture is without governance."
translations.idiomatic: Guyan replied: "I am told that Wang Kan in Deng Prefecture has grown old and ineffective, and that Zheng Xiang in Sui Prefecture governs poorly."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「堪是貞元時御史，只有此一人。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Kan was a censor in the Zhenyuan era—there is only this one man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wang Kan served as a censor under Dezong; he is the only survivor of that generation."

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「臣以王堪舊人，舉為刺史。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: "Your subject, because Kan was an old associate, recommended him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said: "I recommended Wang Kan for a prefecture because he was a veteran official I knew.

sentences.zh: 鄭襄比來守官，亦無敗事。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiang in his recent holding of office likewise has had no failed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zheng Xiang, his recent service has not produced any scandal.

sentences.zh: 若言外郡不理，何止二人？」

translations.literal: If one says the outer prefectures are not well governed, why stop at two men?"
translations.idiomatic: If poorly run provinces were the issue, the problem would involve far more than these two men."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「濟濟多士，文王以寧。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "'With myriad worthy officers, King Wen was secure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quoted: "'With hosts of able men, King Wen found peace.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，班行多閑員，豈時乏才耶？」

translations.literal: In Dezong's time the court ranks had many idle posts—was the age truly lacking talent?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong the official roster was padded with idle posts—was there really a shortage of talent in that age?"

sentences.zh: 李石對曰：「十室之邑，必有忠信。

translations.literal: Li Shi replied: "'In a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi answered: "As the saying goes, even a hamlet of ten households will yield men of loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 安有大國無人？

translations.literal: How could a great state have no men?
translations.idiomatic: How could a great empire lack capable people?

sentences.zh: 蓋貞元中仕進路塞，所以有才之人或托跡他所，此乃不敘進人才之過也。」

translations.literal: It is because in the Zhenyuan era the path of office was blocked, so talented men sometimes took refuge elsewhere—this is the fault of not advancing talented people in order."
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that under Zhenyuan the road to office was blocked, and able men were forced to seek livelihoods elsewhere—that was a failure to promote talent systematically."

sentences.zh: 固言曰：「求才之道，有人保任，便宜獎用。

translations.literal: Guyan said: "In the way of seeking talent, when someone vouches for a man, he should promptly be rewarded with employment.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan said: "The way to find talent is simple: when someone guarantees a candidate, appoint him at once.

sentences.zh: 隨其稱職與否升黜之。」

translations.literal: According to whether he fits his duties, promote or demote him."
translations.idiomatic: Then promote or remove him depending on whether he proves equal to the task."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相薦人，莫計親疏。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When chancellors recommend men, do not reckon closeness or distance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When chancellors recommend officials, kinship should not enter the calculation.

sentences.zh: 竇易直作相，未嘗論用親情。

translations.literal: When Dou Yizhi served as chancellor, he never spoke of employing relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi, during his chancellorship, never once argued for appointing relatives.

sentences.zh: 若己非相才，自宜引退。

translations.literal: If one himself is not material for chancellor, he ought naturally to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: If a man lacks the talent to be chancellor, he should step down on his own.

sentences.zh: 若是公舉，親亦何嫌？

translations.literal: If it is a public recommendation, what scruple is there about kin?
translations.idiomatic: When the nomination is made in the public interest, what objection can there be to a relative?

sentences.zh: 人鮮全才，但用其所長爾。」

translations.literal: Men rarely possess complete talent—one uses only what they excel at."
translations.idiomatic: No one is perfect; employ each man for what he does best."

sentences.zh: 尋進階金紫，判戶部事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to the golden-purple rank and given charge of Ministry of Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to the golden-purple grade and again placed in charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，以門下侍郎平章事出為成都尹、劍南西川節度使，代楊嗣復。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he left office as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor to become Prefect of Chengdu and Military Governor of Jiannan West Circuit, replacing Yang Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: That October he left the chancellorship as vice director of the chancellery and was sent out as prefect of Chengdu and military governor of Jiannan West, succeeding Yang Sifu.

sentences.zh: 上表讓門下侍郎，乃檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining the vice directorship of the Chancellery and was instead made Inspector-General Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to decline the vice directorship of the chancellery and was appointed acting left vice director instead.

sentences.zh: 會昌初入朝，歷兵、戶二部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he entered court and successively served as Minister of War and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang era he returned to court and served in turn as minister of war and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，累授檢校司徒、東都留守、東畿汝都防禦使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he was repeatedly granted the titles Inspector-General Minister of Education, Eastern Capital Garrison Commander, and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Capital and Ruzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Guyan received a series of honors: acting minister of education, eastern capital garrison commander, and defense commissioner for the eastern capital and Ruzhou region.

sentences.zh: 大中末，以太常卿孫簡代之，拜太子太傅，分司東都，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong, Sun Jian as Minister of Ceremonies replaced him; Guyan was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, served in a nominal post at the Eastern Capital, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dazhong era Sun Jian, minister of ceremonies, replaced him; Guyan was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent, held a nominal post in the eastern capital, and died there.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陳、鄭諸公，章疏議論，綽有端士之風。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: Messrs. Chen, Zheng, and the others, in their memorials and deliberations, abundantly possessed the bearing of upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Chen, Zheng, and their colleagues wrote memorials and held debates that marked them as men of upright character.

sentences.zh: 天子待以賢能，付之以鼎職。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven treated them as worthy and able and entrusted them with the tripod offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated them as men of talent and entrusted them with the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 延英獻納，罕聞康濟之謨；

translations.literal: At Yanying audiences offering counsel, plans for wholesome aid were rarely heard;
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanying Hall they offered advice, yet seldom with schemes that truly healed the realm;

sentences.zh: 文陛敷揚，莫副具瞻之望。

translations.literal: On the civil steps they spread their teachings, but did not fulfill the hopes placed in them.
translations.idiomatic: On the palace steps they held forth, yet failed to live up to the nation's expectations.

sentences.zh: 加以互生傾奪，競起愛憎。

translations.literal: Moreover they mutually produced overthrow and seizure, competing to raise love and hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, they undermined one another in factional struggle, driven by personal likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 惟回奉使命而喻籓臣，救危邦而除宿憾。

translations.literal: Only Hui, bearing his commission, went to instruct the frontier ministers, saving a perilous state and removing an old resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Hui, carrying out his mission to reason with the regional commanders, rescued a state in crisis and laid an old grievance to rest.

sentences.zh: 況昭獻文章可以為世範，德行可以為人師，有啟、誦之上才，非桓、靈之失道，詎可不思己過，只務面欺。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhaoxian's writings could serve as a model for the age and his virtue could serve as a teacher for men; he had the superior talent of Qi and Song, and was not a Huan or Ling who lost the Way—how could they not reflect on their own faults and only strive to deceive to his face?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong, posthumously honored as Zhaoxian, offered writings fit to be a model for the age and conduct fit to teach others; he deserved ministers like Qi and Song, not the corrupt age of Emperors Huan and Ling—yet these men refused to examine their own failings and contented themselves with deceiving their ruler to his face.

sentences.zh: 輔弼之宜，安可垂訓？

translations.literal: As befits assisting ministers, how could this be handed down as instruction?
translations.idiomatic: How could such conduct be held up as a model for future chancellors?

sentences.zh: 若俾韓非之言進矣，子輩安可逃乎？

translations.literal: If Han Fei's words were applied, how could you fellows escape?
translations.idiomatic: Had Han Fei's warning about deceitful ministers been heeded, none of you could have escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 土運之衰，斯為魍魎，悲夫！

translations.literal: The earth element's fortune declined—such were specters and goblins. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When the cosmic age waned, these were the demons it produced—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：愛而知惡，憎不忘善。

translations.literal: Praise says: in loving, know evil; in hating, do not forget good.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: to love yet recognize what is wrong, and to dislike yet remember what is good.

sentences.zh: 平心救非，可居鼎鉉。

translations.literal: With a level heart correcting wrongs, one may occupy the tripod cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: With impartial judgment and a willingness to set errors right, one is fit to wield the chancellor's authority.

sentences.zh: 吠聲濟惡，結黨專朝。

translations.literal: Barking at others' voices to aid evil, forming factions to monopolize the court.
translations.idiomatic: Echoing slander to advance wicked ends and forming cliques to dominate the court.

sentences.zh: 謀身壞國。

translations.literal: Scheming for oneself and ruining the state.
translations.idiomatic: They schemed for personal gain and brought the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 何名燮調？

translations.literal: What name of harmonizing adjustment?
translations.idiomatic: What harmony did they ever achieve?
